[210](#210)        debug!("Querying existing columns: {:?}, [{:?}, {:?}]", column_query, &self.schema, &self.collection_id.as_str());
[211](#211)        let rows = client
[212](#212)            .query(&column_query, &[&self.schema, &self.collection_id.as_str()])
[213](#213)            .await
[214](#214)            .map_err(|err| StateError::DDLError(Box::new(err)))?;
[215](#215)        for row in rows {
[216](#216)            let is_nullable: String = row.get("is_nullable");
[217](#217)            new_columns.push(PostgresColumn {
[218](#218)                name: row.get("column_name"),
[219](#219)                is_nullable: is_nullable.eq("YES"),
[220](#220)                data_type: row.get("data_type"),
[221](#221)            })
[222](#222)        }
[223](#223)
[224](#224)        let mut columns = self.columns.write().unwrap();
[225](#225)        *columns = new_columns;
[226](#226)        drop(columns);
[227](#227)
[228](#228)        Ok(())
[229](#229)    }
[230](#230)
[231](#231)    pub fn existing_columns(&self) -> Vec<String> {
[232](#232)        let columns = self.columns.read().unwrap();
[233](#233)        columns.iter().map(|column| column.name.clone()).collect()
[234](#234)    }
[235](#235)
[236](#236)    pub fn column(&self, column_name: &String) -> Option<PostgresColumn> {
[237](#237)        let columns = self.columns.read().unwrap();
[238](#238)        columns.iter().find(|column| column.name == *column_name).cloned()
[239](#239)    }
[240](#240)
[241](#241)    pub fn has_column(&self, column_name: &String) -> bool { self.column(column_name).is_some() }
[242](#242)
[243](#243)    pub async fn create_event_table(&self, client: &mut tokio_postgres::Client) -> Result<(), StateError> {
[244](#244)        let create_query = format!(
[245](#245)            r#"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "{}"(
[246](#246)                "id" character(43) PRIMARY KEY,
[247](#247)                "entity_id" character(22),
[248](#248)                "operations" bytea,
[249](#249)                "parent" character(43)[],
[250](#250)                "attestations" bytea
[251](#251)            )"#,
[252](#252)            self.event_table()
[253](#253)        );
[254](#254)
[255](#255)        debug!("{create_query}");
[256](#256)        client.execute(&create_query, &[]).await.map_err(|e| StateError::DDLError(Box::new(e)))?;
[257](#257)        Ok(())
[258](#258)    }
[259](#259)
[260](#260)    pub async fn create_state_table(&self, client: &mut tokio_postgres::Client) -> Result<(), StateError> {
[261](#261)        let create_query = format!(
[262](#262)            r#"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "{}"(
[263](#263)                "id" character(22) PRIMARY KEY,
[264](#264)                "state_buffer" BYTEA,
[265](#265)                "head" character(43)[],
[266](#266)                "attestations" BYTEA[]
[267](#267)            )"#,
[268](#268)            self.state_table()
[269](#269)        );
[270](#270)
[271](#271)        debug!("{create_query}");
[272](#272)        match client.execute(&create_query, &[]).await {
[273](#273)            Ok(_) => Ok(()),
[274](#274)            Err(err) => {
[275](#275)                if let Some(db_err) = err.as_db_error() {
[277](#277)                    error!("PostgresBucket({}).create_state_table error: {} (code: {:?})", self.collection_id, db_err, db_err.code());
[278](#278)                } else {
[279](#279)                    error!("PostgresBucket({}).create_state_table error: {:?}", self.collection_id, err);
[280](#280)                }
[281](#281)                Err(StateError::DDLError(Box::new(err)))
[282](#282)            }
[283](#283)        }
[284](#284)    }
[285](#285)
[286](#286)    pub async fn add_missing_columns(
[287](#287)        &self,
[288](#288)        client: &mut tokio_postgres::Client,
[289](#289)        missing: Vec<(String, &'static str)>, ) -> Result<(), StateError> {
[291](#291)        if missing.is_empty() {
[292](#292)            return Ok(());
[293](#293)        }
[294](#294)
[295](#295)        let lock_key = acquire_ddl_lock(client, self.collection_id.as_str()).await?;
[297](#297)
[298](#298)        let result = async {
[299](#299)            self.rebuild_columns_cache(client).await?;
[301](#301)
[302](#302)            for (column, datatype) in missing {
[303](#303)                if Postgres::sane_name(&column) && !self.has_column(&column) {
[304](#304)                    let alter_query = format!(r#"ALTER TABLE "{}" ADD COLUMN "{}" {}"#, self.state_table(), column, datatype);
[305](#305)                    info!("PostgresBucket({}).add_missing_columns: {}", self.collection_id, alter_query);
[306](#306)                    match client.execute(&alter_query, &[]).await {
[307](#307)                        Ok(_) => {}
[308](#308)                        Err(err) => {
[309](#309)                            if let Some(db_err) = err.as_db_error() {
[311](#311)                                warn!(
[312](#312)                                    "Error adding column {} to table {}: {} (code: {:?})",
[313](#313)                                    column,
[314](#314)                                    self.state_table(),
[315](#315)                                    db_err,
[316](#316)                                    db_err.code()
[317](#317)                                );
[318](#318)                            } else {
[319](#319)                                warn!("Error adding column {} to table {}: {:?}", column, self.state_table(), err);
[320](#320)                            }
[321](#321)                            self.rebuild_columns_cache(client).await?;
[322](#322)                            return Err(StateError::DDLError(Box::new(err)));
[323](#323)                        }
[324](#324)                    }
[325](#325)                }
[326](#326)            }
[327](#327)
[328](#328)            self.rebuild_columns_cache(client).await?;
[329](#329)            Ok(())
[330](#330)        }
[331](#331)        .await;
[332](#332)
[333](#333)        release_ddl_lock(client, lock_key).await?;
[335](#335)
[336](#336)        result
[337](#337)    }
[338](#338)}
[339](#339)
[340](#340)#[async_trait]
[341](#341)impl StorageCollection for PostgresBucket {
[342](#342)    async fn set_state(&self, state: Attested<EntityState>) -> Result<bool, MutationError> {
[343](#343)        let state_buffers = bincode::serialize(&state.payload.state.state_buffers)?;
[344](#344)        let attestations: Vec<Vec<u8>> = state.attestations.iter().map(bincode::serialize).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
[345](#345)        let id = state.payload.entity_id;
[346](#346)
[347](#347)        if state.payload.state.head.is_empty() {
[349](#349)            warn!("Warning: Empty head detected for entity {}", id);
[350](#350)        }
[351](#351)
[352](#352)        let mut client = self.pool.get().await.map_err(|err| MutationError::General(err.into()))?;
[353](#353)
[354](#354)        let mut columns: Vec<String> = vec!["id".to_owned(), "state_buffer".to_owned(), "head".to_owned(), "attestations".to_owned()];
[355](#355)        let mut params: Vec<&(dyn ToSql + Sync)> = Vec::new();
[356](#356)        params.push(&id);
[357](#357)        params.push(&state_buffers);
[358](#358)        params.push(&state.payload.state.head);
[359](#359)        params.push(&attestations);
[360](#360)
[361](#361)        let mut materialized: Vec<(String, Option<PGValue>)> = Vec::new();
[362](#362)        let mut seen_properties = std::collections::HashSet::new();
[363](#363)
[364](#364)        for (name, state_buffer) in state.payload.state.state_buffers.iter() {
[366](#366)            let backend = backend_from_string(name, Some(state_buffer))?;
[367](#367)            for (column, value) in backend.property_values() {
[368](#368)                if !seen_properties.insert(column.clone()) {
[369](#369)                    continue;
[374](#374)                }
[375](#375)
[376](#376)                let pg_value: Option<PGValue> = value.map(|value| value.into());
[377](#377)                if !self.has_column(&column) {
[378](#378)                    if let Some(ref pg_value) = pg_value {
[380](#380)                        self.add_missing_columns(&mut client, vec![(column.clone(), pg_value.postgres_type())]).await?;
[381](#381)                    } else {
[382](#382)                        continue;
[386](#386)                    }
[387](#387)                }
[388](#388)
[389](#389)                materialized.push((column.clone(), pg_value));
[390](#390)            }
[391](#391)        }
[392](#392)
[393](#393)        for (name, parameter) in &materialized {
[394](#394)            columns.push(name.clone());
[395](#395)
[396](#396)            match ¶meter {
[397](#397)                Some(value) => match value {
[398](#398)                    PGValue::CharacterVarying(string) => params.push(string),
[399](#399)                    PGValue::SmallInt(number) => params.push(number),
[400](#400)                    PGValue::Integer(number) => params.push(number),
[401](#401)                    PGValue::BigInt(number) => params.push(number),
[402](#402)                    PGValue::DoublePrecision(float) => params.push(float),
[403](#403)                    PGValue::Bytea(bytes) => params.push(bytes),
[404](#404)                    PGValue::Boolean(bool) => params.push(bool),
[405](#405)                    PGValue::Jsonb(json_val) => params.push(json_val),
[406](#406)                },
[407](#407)                None => params.push(&UntypedNull),
[408](#408)            }
[409](#409)        }
[410](#410)        let columns_str = columns.iter().map(|name| format!("\"{}\"", name)).collect::<Vec<String>>().join(", ");
[411](#411)        let values_str = params.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, _)| format!("${}", index + 1)).collect::<Vec<String>>().join(", ");
[412](#412)        let columns_update_str = columns
[413](#413)            .iter()
[414](#414)            .enumerate()
[415](#415)            .skip(1) .map(|(index, name)| format!("\"{}\" = ${}", name, index + 1))
[417](#417)            .collect::<Vec<String>>()
[418](#418)            .join(", ");
[419](#419)
[420](#420)        let query = format!(
[422](#422)            r#"WITH old_state AS (
[423](#423)                SELECT "head" FROM "{0}" WHERE "id" = $1
[424](#424)            )
[425](#425)            INSERT INTO "{0}"({1}) VALUES({2})
[426](#426)            ON CONFLICT("id") DO UPDATE SET {3}
[427](#427)            RETURNING (SELECT "head" FROM old_state) as old_head"#,
[428](#428)            self.state_table(),
[429](#429)            columns_str,
[430](#430)            values_str,
[431](#431)            columns_update_str
[432](#432)        );
[433](#433)
[434](#434)        debug!("PostgresBucket({}).set_state: {}", self.collection_id, query);
[435](#435)        let mut created_table = false;
[436](#436)        let row = loop {
[437](#437)            match client.query_one(&query, params.as_slice()).await {
[438](#438)                Ok(row) => break row,
[439](#439)                Err(err) => {
[440](#440)                    let kind = error_kind(&err);
[441](#441)                    if let ErrorKind::UndefinedTable { table } = kind {
[442](#442)                        if table == self.state_table() && !created_table {
[443](#443)                            self.create_state_table(&mut client).await?;
[444](#444)                            created_table = true;
[445](#445)                            continue; }
[447](#447)                    }
[448](#448)                    return Err(StateError::DDLError(Box::new(err)).into());
[449](#449)                }
[450](#450)            }
[451](#451)        };
[452](#452)
[453](#453)        let old_head: Option<Clock> = row.get("old_head");
[455](#455)        let changed = match old_head {
[456](#456)            None => true, Some(old_head) => old_head != state.payload.state.head,
[458](#458)        };
[459](#459)
[460](#460)        debug!("PostgresBucket({}).set_state: Changed: {}", self.collection_id, changed);
[461](#461)        Ok(changed)
[462](#462)    }
[463](#463)
[464](#464)    async fn get_state(&self, id: EntityId) -> Result<Attested<EntityState>, RetrievalError> {
[465](#465)        let query = format!(r#"SELECT "id", "state_buffer", "head", "attestations" FROM "{}" WHERE "id" = $1"#, self.state_table());
[467](#467)
[468](#468)        let mut client = match self.pool.get().await {
[469](#469)            Ok(client) => client,
[470](#470)            Err(err) => {
[471](#471)                return Err(RetrievalError::StorageError(err.into()));
[472](#472)            }
[473](#473)        };
[474](#474)
[475](#475)        debug!("PostgresBucket({}).get_state: {}", self.collection_id, query);
[476](#476)        let rows = match client.query(&query, &[&id]).await {
[477](#477)            Ok(rows) => rows,
[478](#478)            Err(err) => {
[479](#479)                let kind = error_kind(&err);
[480](#480)                if let ErrorKind::UndefinedTable { table } = kind {
[481](#481)                    if table == self.state_table() {
[482](#482)                        self.create_state_table(&mut client).await.map_err(|e| RetrievalError::StorageError(e.into()))?;
[483](#483)                        return Err(RetrievalError::EntityNotFound(id));
[484](#484)                    }
[485](#485)                }
[486](#486)                return Err(RetrievalError::StorageError(err.into()));
[487](#487)            }
[488](#488)        };
[489](#489)
[490](#490)        let row = match rows.into_iter().next() {
[491](#491)            Some(row) => row,
[492](#492)            None => return Err(RetrievalError::EntityNotFound(id)),
[493](#493)        };
[494](#494)
[495](#495)        debug!("PostgresBucket({}).get_state: Row: {:?}", self.collection_id, row);
[496](#496)        let row_id: EntityId = row.try_get("id").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[497](#497)        assert_eq!(row_id, id);
[498](#498)
[499](#499)        let serialized_buffers: Vec<u8> = row.try_get("state_buffer").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[500](#500)        let state_buffers: BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>> = bincode::deserialize(&serialized_buffers).map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[501](#501)        let head: Clock = row.try_get("head").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[502](#502)        let attestation_bytes: Vec<Vec<u8>> = row.try_get("attestations").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[503](#503)        let attestations = attestation_bytes
[504](#504)            .into_iter()
[505](#505)            .map(|bytes| bincode::deserialize(&bytes))
[506](#506)            .collect::<Result<Vec<Attestation>, _>>()
[507](#507)            .map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[508](#508)
[509](#509)        Ok(Attested {
[510](#510)            payload: EntityState {
[511](#511)                entity_id: id,
[512](#512)                collection: self.collection_id.clone(),
[513](#513)                state: State { state_buffers: StateBuffers(state_buffers), head },
[514](#514)            },
[515](#515)            attestations: AttestationSet(attestations),
[516](#516)        })
[517](#517)    }
[518](#518)
[519](#519)    async fn fetch_states(&self, selection: &ankql::ast::Selection) -> Result<Vec<Attested<EntityState>>, RetrievalError> {
[520](#520)        debug!("fetch_states: {:?}", selection);
[521](#521)        let mut client = self.pool.get().await.map_err(|err| RetrievalError::StorageError(Box::new(err)))?;
[522](#522)
[523](#523)        let referenced = selection.referenced_columns();
[528](#528)        let cached = self.existing_columns();
[529](#529)        let unknown_to_cache: Vec<&String> = referenced.iter().filter(|col| !cached.contains(col)).collect();
[530](#530)
[531](#531)        if !unknown_to_cache.is_empty() {
[533](#533)            debug!("PostgresBucket({}).fetch_states: Unknown columns {:?}, refreshing schema cache", self.collection_id, unknown_to_cache);
[534](#534)            self.rebuild_columns_cache(&mut client).await.map_err(|e| RetrievalError::StorageError(e.into()))?;
[535](#535)        }
[536](#536)
[537](#537)        let existing = self.existing_columns();
[539](#539)        let missing: Vec<String> = referenced.into_iter().filter(|col| !existing.contains(col)).collect();
[540](#540)
[541](#541)        let effective_selection = if missing.is_empty() {
[542](#542)            selection.clone()
[543](#543)        } else {
[544](#544)            debug!("PostgresBucket({}).fetch_states: Columns {:?} don't exist, treating as NULL", self.collection_id, missing);
[545](#545)            selection.assume_null(&missing)
[546](#546)        };
[547](#547)
[548](#548)        let split = sql_builder::split_predicate_for_postgres(&effective_selection.predicate);
[550](#550)        let needs_post_filter = split.needs_post_filter();
[551](#551)        let remaining_predicate = split.remaining_predicate; debug!(
[553](#553)            "PostgresBucket({}).fetch_states: SQL predicate: {:?}, remaining: {:?}, needs_post_filter: {}",
[554](#554)            self.collection_id, split.sql_predicate, remaining_predicate, needs_post_filter
[555](#555)        );
[556](#556)
[557](#557)        #[cfg(debug_assertions)]
[559](#559)        {
[560](#560)            let mut spilled = self.last_spilled_predicate.write().unwrap();
[561](#561)            *spilled = if needs_post_filter { Some(remaining_predicate.clone()) } else { None };
[562](#562)        }
[563](#563)
[564](#564)        #[cfg(debug_assertions)]
[566](#566)        {
[567](#567)            let spilled = if needs_post_filter { Some(remaining_predicate.clone()) } else { None };
[568](#568)            *self.last_spilled_predicate.write().unwrap() = spilled;
[569](#569)        }
[570](#570)
[571](#571)        let sql_selection = ankql::ast::Selection {
[573](#573)            predicate: split.sql_predicate,
[574](#574)            order_by: effective_selection.order_by.clone(),
[575](#575)            limit: if needs_post_filter {
[576](#576)                None } else {
[578](#578)                effective_selection.limit
[579](#579)            },
[580](#580)        };
[581](#581)
[582](#582)        let mut results = Vec::new();
[583](#583)        let mut builder = SqlBuilder::with_fields(vec!["id", "state_buffer", "head", "attestations"]);
[584](#584)        builder.table_name(self.state_table());
[585](#585)        builder.selection(&sql_selection)?;
[586](#586)
[587](#587)        let (sql, args) = builder.build()?;
[588](#588)        debug!("PostgresBucket({}).fetch_states: SQL: {} with args: {:?}", self.collection_id, sql, args);
[589](#589)
[590](#590)        let stream = match client.query_raw(&sql, args).await {
[591](#591)            Ok(stream) => stream,
[592](#592)            Err(err) => {
[593](#593)                let kind = error_kind(&err);
[594](#594)                if let ErrorKind::UndefinedTable { table } = kind {
[595](#595)                    if table == self.state_table() {
[596](#596)                        return Ok(Vec::new());
[598](#598)                    }
[599](#599)                }
[600](#600)                return Err(RetrievalError::StorageError(err.into()));
[601](#601)            }
[602](#602)        };
[603](#603)        pin_mut!(stream);
[604](#604)
[605](#605)        while let Some(row) = stream.try_next().await.map_err(RetrievalError::storage)? {
[606](#606)            let id: EntityId = row.try_get(0).map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[607](#607)            let state_buffer: Vec<u8> = row.try_get(1).map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[608](#608)            let state_buffers: BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>> = bincode::deserialize(&state_buffer).map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[609](#609)            let head: Clock = row.try_get("head").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[610](#610)            let attestation_bytes: Vec<Vec<u8>> = row.try_get("attestations").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[611](#611)            let attestations = attestation_bytes
[612](#612)                .into_iter()
[613](#613)                .map(|bytes| bincode::deserialize(&bytes))
[614](#614)                .collect::<Result<Vec<Attestation>, _>>()
[615](#615)                .map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[616](#616)
[617](#617)            results.push(Attested {
[618](#618)                payload: EntityState {
[619](#619)                    entity_id: id,
[620](#620)                    collection: self.collection_id.clone(),
[621](#621)                    state: State { state_buffers: StateBuffers(state_buffers), head },
[622](#622)                },
[623](#623)                attestations: AttestationSet(attestations),
[624](#624)            });
[625](#625)        }
[626](#626)
[627](#627)        let results = if needs_post_filter {
[629](#629)            debug!(
[630](#630)                "PostgresBucket({}).fetch_states: Post-filtering {} results with remaining predicate",
[631](#631)                self.collection_id,
[632](#632)                results.len()
[633](#633)            );
[634](#634)            let filtered = post_filter_states(&results, &remaining_predicate, &self.collection_id);
[635](#635)
[636](#636)            if let Some(limit) = effective_selection.limit {
[638](#638)                filtered.into_iter().take(limit as usize).collect()
[639](#639)            } else {
[640](#640)                filtered
[641](#641)            }
[642](#642)        } else {
[643](#643)            results
[644](#644)        };
[645](#645)
[646](#646)        Ok(results)
[647](#647)    }
[648](#648)
[649](#649)    async fn add_event(&self, entity_event: &Attested<Event>) -> Result<bool, MutationError> {
[650](#650)        let operations = bincode::serialize(&entity_event.payload.operations)?;
[651](#651)        let attestations = bincode::serialize(&entity_event.attestations)?;
[652](#652)
[653](#653)        let query = format!(
[654](#654)            r#"INSERT INTO "{0}"("id", "entity_id", "operations", "parent", "attestations") VALUES($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)
[655](#655)               ON CONFLICT ("id") DO NOTHING"#,
[656](#656)            self.event_table(),
[657](#657)        );
[658](#658)
[659](#659)        let mut client = self.pool.get().await.map_err(|err| MutationError::General(err.into()))?;
[660](#660)        debug!("PostgresBucket({}).add_event: {}", self.collection_id, query);
[661](#661)        let mut created_table = false;
[662](#662)        let affected = loop {
[663](#663)            match client
[664](#664)                .execute(
[665](#665)                    &query,
[666](#666)                    &[
[667](#667)                        &entity_event.payload.id(),
[668](#668)                        &entity_event.payload.entity_id,
[669](#669)                        &operations,
[670](#670)                        &entity_event.payload.parent,
[671](#671)                        &attestations,
[672](#672)                    ],
[673](#673)                )
[674](#674)                .await
[675](#675)            {
[676](#676)                Ok(affected) => break affected,
[677](#677)                Err(err) => {
[678](#678)                    let kind = error_kind(&err);
[679](#679)                    if let ErrorKind::UndefinedTable { table } = kind {
[680](#680)                        if table == self.event_table() && !created_table {
[681](#681)                            self.create_event_table(&mut client).await?;
[682](#682)                            created_table = true;
[683](#683)                            continue; }
[685](#685)                    }
[686](#686)                    error!("PostgresBucket({}).add_event: Error: {:?}", self.collection_id, err);
[687](#687)                    return Err(StateError::DMLError(Box::new(err)).into());
[688](#688)                }
[689](#689)            }
[690](#690)        };
[691](#691)
[692](#692)        Ok(affected > 0)
[693](#693)    }
[694](#694)
[695](#695)    async fn get_events(&self, event_ids: Vec<EventId>) -> Result<Vec<Attested<Event>>, RetrievalError> {
[696](#696)        if event_ids.is_empty() {
[697](#697)            return Ok(Vec::new());
[698](#698)        }
[699](#699)
[700](#700)        let query = format!(
[701](#701)            r#"SELECT "id", "entity_id", "operations", "parent", "attestations" FROM "{0}" WHERE "id" = ANY($1)"#,
[702](#702)            self.event_table(),
[703](#703)        );
[704](#704)
[705](#705)        let client = self.pool.get().await.map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[706](#706)        let rows = match client.query(&query, &[&event_ids]).await {
[707](#707)            Ok(rows) => rows,
[708](#708)            Err(err) => {
[709](#709)                let kind = error_kind(&err);
[710](#710)                match kind {
[711](#711)                    ErrorKind::UndefinedTable { table } if table == self.event_table() => return Ok(Vec::new()),
[712](#712)                    _ => return Err(RetrievalError::storage(err)),
[713](#713)                }
[714](#714)            }
[715](#715)        };
[716](#716)
[717](#717)        let mut events = Vec::new();
[718](#718)        for row in rows {
[719](#719)            let entity_id: EntityId = row.try_get("entity_id").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[720](#720)            let operations: OperationSet = row.try_get("operations").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[721](#721)            let parent: Clock = row.try_get("parent").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[722](#722)            let attestations_binary: Vec<u8> = row.try_get("attestations").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[723](#723)            let attestations: Vec<Attestation> = bincode::deserialize(&attestations_binary).map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[724](#724)
[725](#725)            let event = Attested {
[726](#726)                payload: Event { collection: self.collection_id.clone(), entity_id, operations, parent },
[727](#727)                attestations: AttestationSet(attestations),
[728](#728)            };
[729](#729)            events.push(event);
[730](#730)        }
[731](#731)        Ok(events)
[732](#732)    }
[733](#733)
[734](#734)    async fn dump_entity_events(&self, entity_id: EntityId) -> Result<Vec<Attested<Event>>, ankurah_core::error::RetrievalError> {
[735](#735)        let query =
[736](#736)            format!(r#"SELECT "id", "operations", "parent", "attestations" FROM "{0}" WHERE "entity_id" = $1"#, self.event_table(),);
[737](#737)
[738](#738)        let client = self.pool.get().await.map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[739](#739)        debug!("PostgresBucket({}).get_events: {}", self.collection_id, query);
[740](#740)        let rows = match client.query(&query, &[&entity_id]).await {
[741](#741)            Ok(rows) => rows,
[742](#742)            Err(err) => {
[743](#743)                let kind = error_kind(&err);
[744](#744)                if let ErrorKind::UndefinedTable { table } = kind {
[745](#745)                    if table == self.event_table() {
[746](#746)                        return Ok(Vec::new());
[747](#747)                    }
[748](#748)                }
[749](#749)
[750](#750)                return Err(RetrievalError::storage(err));
[751](#751)            }
[752](#752)        };
[753](#753)
[754](#754)        let mut events = Vec::new();
[755](#755)        for row in rows {
[756](#756)            let operations_binary: Vec<u8> = row.try_get("operations").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[758](#758)            let operations = bincode::deserialize(&operations_binary).map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[759](#759)            let parent: Clock = row.try_get("parent").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[760](#760)            let attestations_binary: Vec<u8> = row.try_get("attestations").map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[761](#761)            let attestations: Vec<Attestation> = bincode::deserialize(&attestations_binary).map_err(RetrievalError::storage)?;
[762](#762)
[763](#763)            events.push(Attested {
[764](#764)                payload: Event { collection: self.collection_id.clone(), entity_id, operations, parent },
[765](#765)                attestations: AttestationSet(attestations),
[766](#766)            });
[767](#767)        }
[768](#768)
[769](#769)        Ok(events)
[770](#770)    }
[771](#771)}
[772](#772)
[773](#773)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
[777](#777)pub enum ErrorKind {
[778](#778)    RowCount,
[779](#779)    UndefinedTable { table: String },
[780](#780)    UndefinedColumn { table: Option<String>, column: String },
[781](#781)    Unknown,
[782](#782)    PostgresError(String),
[783](#783)}
[784](#784)
[785](#785)pub fn error_kind(err: &tokio_postgres::Error) -> ErrorKind {
[786](#786)    let string = err.as_db_error().map(|e| e.message()).unwrap_or_default().trim().to_owned();
[787](#787)    let _db_error = err.as_db_error();
[788](#788)    let sql_code = err.code().cloned();
[789](#789)
[790](#790)    let err_string = err.to_string();
[792](#792)    if err_string.contains("query returned an unexpected number of rows") || string == "query returned an unexpected number of rows" {
[793](#793)        return ErrorKind::RowCount;
[794](#794)    }
[795](#795)
[796](#796)    debug!("postgres error: {:?}", err);
[803](#803)
[804](#804)    let quote_indices = |s: &str| {
[805](#805)        let mut quotes = Vec::new();
[806](#806)        for (index, char) in s.char_indices() {
[807](#807)            if char == '"' {
[808](#808)                quotes.push(index)
[809](#809)            }
[810](#810)        }
[811](#811)        quotes
[812](#812)    };
[813](#813)
[814](#814)    match sql_code {
[815](#815)        Some(SqlState::UNDEFINED_TABLE) => {
[816](#816)            let quotes = quote_indices(&string);
[818](#818)            if quotes.len() >= 2 {
[819](#819)                let table = &string[quotes[0] + 1..quotes[1]];
[820](#820)                ErrorKind::UndefinedTable { table: table.to_owned() }
[821](#821)            } else {
[822](#822)                ErrorKind::PostgresError(string.clone())
[823](#823)            }
[824](#824)        }
[825](#825)        Some(SqlState::UNDEFINED_COLUMN) => {
[826](#826)            let quotes = quote_indices(&string);
[830](#830)            if quotes.len() >= 2 {
[831](#831)                let column = string[quotes[0] + 1..quotes[1]].to_owned();
[832](#832)
[833](#833)                let table = if quotes.len() >= 4 {
[834](#834)                    Some(string[quotes[2] + 1..quotes[3]].to_owned())
[836](#836)                } else {
[837](#837)                    None
[839](#839)                };
[840](#840)
[841](#841)                ErrorKind::UndefinedColumn { table, column }
[842](#842)            } else {
[843](#843)                ErrorKind::PostgresError(string.clone())
[844](#844)            }
[845](#845)        }
[846](#846)        _ => ErrorKind::Unknown,
[847](#847)    }
[848](#848)}

[860](#860)fn post_filter_states(
[865](#865)    states: &[Attested<EntityState>],
[866](#866)    predicate: &ankql::ast::Predicate,
[867](#867)    collection_id: &CollectionId,
[868](#868)) -> Vec<Attested<EntityState>> {
[869](#869)    use ankurah_core::entity::TemporaryEntity;
[870](#870)    use ankurah_core::selection::filter::evaluate_predicate;
[871](#871)
[872](#872)    states
[873](#873)        .iter()
[874](#874)        .filter(|attested| {
[875](#875)            match TemporaryEntity::new(attested.payload.entity_id, collection_id.clone(), &attested.payload.state) {
[877](#877)                Ok(temp_entity) => {
[878](#878)                    match evaluate_predicate(&temp_entity, predicate) {
[880](#880)                        Ok(true) => true,
[881](#881)                        Ok(false) => false,
[882](#882)                        Err(e) => {
[883](#883)                            warn!("Post-filter evaluation error for entity {}: {}", attested.payload.entity_id, e);
[884](#884)                            false }
[886](#886)                    }
[887](#887)                }
[888](#888)                Err(e) => {
[889](#889)                    warn!("Failed to create TemporaryEntity for post-filtering {}: {}", attested.payload.entity_id, e);
[890](#890)                    false }
[892](#892)            }
[893](#893)        })
[894](#894)        .cloned()
[895](#895)        .collect()
[896](#896)}

# fakecloud-k8s 0.31.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fakecloud-k8s/0.31.0

Shared Kubernetes-backend primitives for FakeCloud.

FakeCloud can run its container-backed services (Lambda, ElastiCache,
RDS, ECS) either by shelling out to a local Docker/Podman daemon (the
default) or by spawning native Pods in a Kubernetes cluster. The k8s
path is the same for every service — connect a client, build a Pod,
wait for it to come up, optionally `exec` into it, tear it down, and
reap orphans left by a previous process. This crate holds that common
machinery so each service only has to describe *its* Pod, not
re-implement the client bootstrap, readiness polling, exec plumbing,
reaping, and DNS-safe naming.

Backend selection (`FAKECLOUD_CONTAINER_BACKEND` /
`FAKECLOUD_<SERVICE>_BACKEND`) lives in [`backend`]. The kube client
wrapper and Pod lifecycle live in [`client`]. Env parsing
(`FAKECLOUD_K8S_*`) lives in [`env`]. Operator-configurable Pod
scheduling/metadata (node selector, tolerations, annotations) lives in
[`pod_config`]. Naming + label conventions live in [`names`] and
[`labels`].

See `website/content/docs/guides/kubernetes-backend.md` for the
operator-facing setup (ServiceAccount, RBAC, Deployment yaml).

---

# k8s_openapi - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/k8s-openapi/^0.23/

## Expand description

Bindings for the Kubernetes client API, generated from the OpenAPI spec.

Each supported version of Kubernetes is represented by a feature name (like `v1_9`). Only one such feature can be enabled at a time.

These docs have been generated with the `v1_31` feature enabled. To see docs for one of the other supported versions, please generate the docs locally with `cargo doc --features 'v1_<>'`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#resources)Resources

This example creates an instance of [ api::core::v1::PodSpec](https://docs.rs/api/core/v1/struct.PodSpec.html) with no other properties set, and pretty-prints it.

```
use k8s_openapi::api::core::v1 as api;
fn main() {
    let pod_spec: api::PodSpec = Default::default();
    println!("{pod_spec:#?}");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate features

This crate contains several `v1_*` features. Enabling one of the `v1_*` features selects which version of the Kubernetes API server this crate should target.
For example, enabling the `v1_50` feature means the crate will only contain the API exposed by Kubernetes 1.50. It will not expose API
that were removed in 1.50 or earlier, nor any API added in 1.51 or later.

One and only one of the `v1_*` features must be enabled at the same time, otherwise the crate will not compile. This ensures that all crates in the crate graph
use the same types. If it was possible for one library crate to use `api::core::v1::Pod` corresponding to v1.50 and another to use the type
corresponding to v1.51, an application would not be able to use the same `Pod` value with both.

Thus, it is recommended that only application crates must enable one of the `v1_*` features, corresponding to the version of Kubernetes
that the application wants to support.

```
# For application crates
[dependencies]
k8s-openapi = { version = "...", features = ["v1_50"] }
```
If you’re writing a library crate, your crate *must not* enable any features of `k8s-openapi` directly. The choice of which feature to enable
must be left to any application crates that use your library. This ensures that all `k8s-openapi`-using dependencies in that application crate’s dependency graph
use the same set of `k8s-openapi` types and are interoperable.

If your library crate has tests or examples, you should also add a dev-dependency on `k8s-openapi` in addition to the direct dependency,
and enable a version feature only for that dev-dependency.

```
# For library crates
[dependencies]
k8s-openapi = "..."
[dev-dependencies]
k8s-openapi = { version = "...", features = ["v1_50"] }
```
However, commands like `cargo check` and `cargo doc` do not build dev dependencies, so they will not enable the feature and will fail to build. There are two ways
you can resolve this:

-
Add a feature to your library that enables one of the k8s-openapi `v1_*`features, and then remember to enable this feature when running such commands.`[features] __check = ["k8s-openapi/v1_50"]``$ cargo check --features __check`
-
Define the `K8S_OPENAPI_ENABLED_VERSION`env var when running such commands:`$ K8S_OPENAPI_ENABLED_VERSION=1.50 cargo check`

[§](https://docs.rs#conditional-compilation)Conditional compilation

As the previous section explained, library crates must not enable any version features in their `k8s-openapi` dependency. However, your library crate may
need to know about which version gets selected eventually.

For example:

-
Your crate creates a `PodSecurityContext`and wants to set the`supplemental_groups_policy`field. This field is only available in Kubernetes 1.31+, so you want your crate to fail to compile if a lower feature was enabled.
-
Your crate creates a `PodSecurityContext`and wants to set the`supplemental_groups_policy`field, but it’s okay to not set it when compiling for older versions.

There are two ways for your crate to determine which feature of `k8s-openapi` is enabled:

-
The `k8s-openapi`crate exports`k8s_if_*`macros,With these macros, the two cases above would be solved like this: -
[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)`// The compile_error!() is only emitted if 1.30 or lower is selected. k8s_openapi::k8s_if_le_1_30! { compile_error!("This crate requires the v1_31 (or higher) feature to be enabled on the k8s-openapi crate."); } ... let pod_security_context = k8s_openapi::api::core::v1::PodSecurityContext { supplemental_groups_policy: ..., ... };`

-
-
The `k8s-openapi`crate emits the selected version number as metadata that your crate can read in a build script from the`DEP_K8S_OPENAPI_*_VERSION`env var.`// Your crate's build.rs fn main() { let k8s_openapi_version: u32 = std::env::vars_os() .find_map(|(key, value)| { let key = key.into_string().ok()?; if key.starts_with("DEP_K8S_OPENAPI_") && key.ends_with("_VERSION") { let value = value.into_string().ok()?; Some(value) } else { None } }).expect("DEP_K8S_OPENAPI_*_VERSION must have been set by k8s-openapi") .parse().expect("DEP_K8S_OPENAPI_*_VERSION is malformed"); // k8s_openapi_version has the format 0x00_MM_NN_00. // // - MM is the major version. // - NN is the minor version. // // Thus, if the v1_31 feature was enabled, k8s_openapi_version would be 0x00_01_1F_00 // The build script can now do arbitrary things with the information. // For example, it could define custom cfgs: if k8s_openapi_version >= 0x00_01_1F_00 { println!(r#"cargo::rustc-cfg=k8s_pod_security_context_supports_supplemental_groups_policy"#); } // ... or emit new source code files under OUT_DIR, or anything else a build script can do. }`With this cfg, the two cases above would be solved like this: -
[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)`// The compile_error!() is only emitted if 1.30 or lower is selected. #[cfg(not(k8s_pod_security_context_supports_supplemental_groups_policy))] compile_error!("This crate requires the v1_31 (or higher) feature to be enabled on the k8s-openapi crate."); ... let pod_security_context = k8s_openapi::api::core::v1::PodSecurityContext { supplemental_groups_policy: ..., ... };`

-

Note that both approaches require your crate to have a direct dependency on the `k8s-openapi` crate. Neither approach is available if your crate
only has a transitive dependency on the `k8s-openapi` crate.

The macros approach is easier to use since it doesn’t require a build script.

The build script method lets you emit arbitrary cfgs, emit arbitrary source code, and generally gives you more options, at the cost of needing a build script.
`cfg()`s can be used in places where macros cannot, such as how the second example above shows it being used on a single field in a struct literal.

[§](https://docs.rs#custom-resource-definitions)Custom resource definitions

The [ k8s-openapi-derive crate](https://crates.io/crates/k8s-openapi-derive) provides a custom derive for generating clientsets
for custom resources. See that crate’s docs for more information.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- Strategies for merging collections.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- This macro evaluates to its contents if the`v1_30`or higher feature is enabled, otherwise it evaluates to nothing.

- This macro evaluates to its contents if the`v1_30`or lower feature is enabled, otherwise it evaluates to nothing.

- A macro that emits a`match`expr with the given test expression and arms. The match arms can be annotated with the other conditional compilation macros in this crate so that they’re only emitted if the predicate is true.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

# kube - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kube/^0.95/

## Expand description

Kube is an umbrella-crate for interacting with [Kubernetes](http://kubernetes.io) in Rust.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

Kube contains a Kubernetes client, a controller runtime, a custom resource derive, and various tooling required for building applications or controllers that interact with Kubernetes.

The main modules are:

- `client`- `Client`
- `config`- `Config`
- `api`- `Api`
- `derive`- `CustomResource`- `Resource`
- `runtime`- `Controller`- `watcher`- `reflector`- `Store`
- `core`- `apimachinery`

You can use each of these as you need with the help of the [exported features](https://kube.rs/features/).

[§](https://docs.rs#using-the-client)Using the Client

```
use futures::{StreamExt, TryStreamExt};
use kube::{Client, api::{Api, ResourceExt, ListParams, PostParams}};
use k8s_openapi::api::core::v1::Pod;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // Infer the runtime environment and try to create a Kubernetes Client
    let client = Client::try_default().await?;
    // Read pods in the configured namespace into the typed interface from k8s-openapi
    let pods: Api<Pod> = Api::default_namespaced(client);
    for p in pods.list(&ListParams::default()).await? {
        println!("found pod {}", p.name_any());
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
For details, see:

- `Client`
- `Api`
- [k8s-openapi](https://docs.rs/k8s-openapi/*/k8s_openapi/)for documentation about the generated Kubernetes types

[§](https://docs.rs#using-the-runtime-with-the-derive-macro)Using the Runtime with the Derive macro

```
use schemars::JsonSchema;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::json;
use futures::{StreamExt, TryStreamExt};
use k8s_openapi::apiextensions_apiserver::pkg::apis::apiextensions::v1::CustomResourceDefinition;
use kube::{
    api::{Api, DeleteParams, PatchParams, Patch, ResourceExt},
    core::CustomResourceExt,
    Client, CustomResource,
    runtime::{watcher, WatchStreamExt, wait::{conditions, await_condition}},
};
// Our custom resource
#[derive(CustomResource, Deserialize, Serialize, Clone, Debug, JsonSchema)]
#[kube(group = "clux.dev", version = "v1", kind = "Foo", namespaced)]
pub struct FooSpec {
    info: String,
    #[schemars(length(min = 3))]
    name: String,
    replicas: i32,
}
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let client = Client::try_default().await?;
    let crds: Api<CustomResourceDefinition> = Api::all(client.clone());
    // Apply the CRD so users can create Foo instances in Kubernetes
    crds.patch("foos.clux.dev",
        &PatchParams::apply("my_manager"),
        &Patch::Apply(Foo::crd())
    ).await?;
    // Wait for the CRD to be ready
    tokio::time::timeout(
        std::time::Duration::from_secs(10),
        await_condition(crds, "foos.clux.dev", conditions::is_crd_established())
    ).await?;
    // Watch for changes to foos in the configured namespace
    let foos: Api<Foo> = Api::default_namespaced(client.clone());
    let wc = watcher::Config::default();
    let mut apply_stream = watcher(foos, wc).applied_objects().boxed();
    while let Some(f) = apply_stream.try_next().await? {
        println!("saw apply to {}", f.name_any());
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
For details, see:

- `CustomResource`
- `runtime::watcher`- `Api::watch`
- `runtime`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

A large list of complete, runnable examples with explainations are available in the [examples folder](https://github.com/kube-rs/kube/tree/main/examples).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- API helpers for structured interaction with the Kubernetes API
- API client for interacting with the Kubernetes API
- Kubernetes configuration objects.
- Types and traits necessary for interacting with the Kubernetes API
- High-level utilities for runtime API discovery.
- Error handling and error types
- A prelude for kube. Reduces the number of duplicated imports.
- Common components for building Kubernetes operators

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- The generic Api abstraction
- Client for connecting with a Kubernetes cluster.
- Configuration object for accessing a Kuernetes cluster
- A caching client for running API discovery against the Kubernetes API.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- Extension trait that is implemented by kube-derive
- An accessor trait for a kubernetes Resource.
- Helper methods for resources.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- Convient alias for`Result<T, Error>`

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- A custom derive for kubernetes custom resource definitions.
- A custom derive for inheriting Resource impl for the type.

# reqwest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reqwest/^0.13/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#reqwest)reqwest

The `reqwest` crate provides a convenient, higher-level HTTP
[ Client](https://docs.rs/struct.Client.html).

It handles many of the things that most people just expect an HTTP client to do for them.

- Async and [blocking](https://docs.rs/blocking/index.html)Clients
- Plain bodies, [JSON](https://docs.rs#json),[urlencoded](https://docs.rs#forms),[multipart](https://docs.rs/multipart/index.html)
- Customizable [redirect policy](https://docs.rs#redirect-policies)
- HTTP [Proxies](https://docs.rs#proxies)
- Uses [TLS](https://docs.rs#tls)by default
- Cookies

The [ reqwest::Client](https://docs.rs/struct.Client.html) is asynchronous (requiring Tokio). For
applications wishing  to only make a few HTTP requests, the

[API may be more convenient.](https://docs.rs/blocking/index.html)

`reqwest::blocking`Additional learning resources include:

[§](https://docs.rs#commercial-support)Commercial Support

For private advice, support, reviews, access to the maintainer, and the
like, reach out for [commercial support](https://seanmonstar.com/sponsor).

[§](https://docs.rs#making-a-get-request)Making a GET request

For a single request, you can use the [ get](https://docs.rs/fn.get.html) shortcut method.

```
let body = reqwest::get("https://www.rust-lang.org")
    .await?
    .text()
    .await?;
println!("body = {body:?}");
```
**NOTE**: If you plan to perform multiple requests, it is best to create a
[ Client](https://docs.rs/struct.Client.html) and reuse it, taking advantage of keep-alive connection
pooling.

[§](https://docs.rs#making-post-requests-or-setting-request-bodies)Making POST requests (or setting request bodies)

There are several ways you can set the body of a request. The basic one is
by using the `body()` method of a [ RequestBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.RequestBuilder.html). This lets you set the
exact raw bytes of what the body should be. It accepts various types,
including

`String` and `Vec<u8>`. If you wish to pass a custom
type, you can use the `reqwest::Body` constructors.```
let client = reqwest::Client::new();
let res = client.post("http://httpbin.org/post")
    .body("the exact body that is sent")
    .send()
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#forms)Forms

It’s very common to want to send form data in a request body. This can be done with any type that can be serialized into form data.

This can be an array of tuples, or a `HashMap`, or a custom type that
implements [ Serialize](http://serde.rs).

The feature `form` is required.

```
// This will POST a body of `foo=bar&baz=quux`
let params = [("foo", "bar"), ("baz", "quux")];
let client = reqwest::Client::new();
let res = client.post("http://httpbin.org/post")
    .form(¶ms)
    .send()
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#json)JSON

There is also a `json` method helper on the [ RequestBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.RequestBuilder.html) that works in
a similar fashion the

`form` method. It can take any value that can be
serialized into JSON.The feature `json` is required.

```
// This will POST a body of `{"lang":"rust","body":"json"}`
let mut map = HashMap::new();
map.insert("lang", "rust");
map.insert("body", "json");
let client = reqwest::Client::new();
let res = client.post("http://httpbin.org/post")
    .json(&map)
    .send()
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#redirect-policies)Redirect Policies

By default, a `Client` will automatically handle HTTP redirects, having a
maximum redirect chain of 10 hops. To customize this behavior, a
[ redirect::Policy](https://docs.rs/redirect/index.html) can be used with a

`ClientBuilder`.[§](https://docs.rs#cookies)Cookies

The automatic storing and sending of session cookies can be enabled with
the [ cookie_store](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientBuilder.html#method.cookie_store) method on

`ClientBuilder`.[§](https://docs.rs#proxies)Proxies

**NOTE**: System proxies are enabled by default.

System proxies look in environment variables to set HTTP or HTTPS proxies.

`HTTP_PROXY` or `http_proxy` provide HTTP proxies for HTTP connections while
`HTTPS_PROXY` or `https_proxy` provide HTTPS proxies for HTTPS connections.
`ALL_PROXY` or `all_proxy` provide proxies for both HTTP and HTTPS connections.
If both the all proxy and HTTP or HTTPS proxy variables are set the more specific
HTTP or HTTPS proxies take precedence.

These can be overwritten by adding a [ Proxy](https://docs.rs/struct.Proxy.html) to

`ClientBuilder`
i.e. `let proxy = reqwest::Proxy::http("https://secure.example")?;`
or disabled by calling `ClientBuilder::no_proxy()`.`socks` feature is required if you have configured socks proxy like this:

`export https_proxy=socks5://127.0.0.1:1086`[§](https://docs.rs#tls)TLS

A `Client` will use transport layer security (TLS) by default to connect to
HTTPS destinations.

- Additional server certificates can be configured on a `ClientBuilder`with the`Certificate`
- Client certificates can be added to a `ClientBuilder`with the`Identity`
- Various parts of TLS can also be configured or even disabled on the
`ClientBuilder`.

See more details in the [ tls](https://docs.rs/tls/index.html) module.

[§](https://docs.rs#wasm)WASM

The Client implementation automatically switches to the WASM one when the target_arch is wasm32,
the usage is basically the same as the async api. Some of the features are disabled in wasm
: [ tls](https://docs.rs/tls/index.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/cookie/index.html)

`cookie`[, as well as various](https://docs.rs/blocking/index.html)

`blocking``ClientBuilder` methods such as `timeout()` and `connector_layer()`.TLS and cookies are provided through the browser environment, so reqwest can issue TLS requests with cookies, but has limited configuration.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional Features

The following are a list of [Cargo features](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-features-section) that can be
enabled or disabled:

- **http2**- *(enabled by default)*: Enables HTTP/2 support.
- **default-tls**- *(enabled by default)*: Provides TLS support to connect over HTTPS.
- **rustls**: Enables TLS functionality provided by- `rustls`.
- **rustls-no-provider**: Enables TLS provided by- `rustls`without specifying a crypto provider.
- **native-tls**: Enables TLS functionality provided by- `native-tls`.
- **native-tls-vendored**: Enables the- `vendored`feature of- `native-tls`.
- **native-tls-no-alpn**: Enables- `native-tls`without its- `alpn`feature.
- **native-tls-vendored-no-alpn**: Enables- `native-tls-vendored`without its- `alpn`feature.
- **blocking**: Provides the- [blocking](https://docs.rs/blocking/index.html)client API.
- **charset**- *(enabled by default)*: Improved support for decoding text.
- **cookies**: Provides cookie session support.
- **gzip**: Provides response body gzip decompression.
- **brotli**: Provides response body brotli decompression.
- **zstd**: Provides response body zstd decompression.
- **deflate**: Provides response body deflate decompression.
- **query**: Provides query parameter serialization.
- **form**: Provides form data serialization.
- **json**: Provides serialization and deserialization for JSON bodies.
- **multipart**: Provides functionality for multipart forms.
- **stream**: Adds support for- `futures::Stream`.
- **socks**: Provides SOCKS5 proxy support.
- **hickory-dns**: Enables a hickory-dns async resolver instead of default threadpool using- `getaddrinfo`.
- **system-proxy**- *(enabled by default)*: Use Windows and macOS system proxy settings automatically.

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable Features

Some feature flags require additional opt-in by the application, by setting
a `reqwest_unstable` flag.

- **http3**- *(unstable)*: Enables support for sending HTTP/3 requests.

These features are unstable, and experimental. Details about them may be changed in patch releases.

You can pass such a flag to the compiler via `.cargo/config`, or
environment variables, such as:

`RUSTFLAGS="--cfg reqwest_unstable" cargo build`[§](https://docs.rs#sponsors)Sponsors

Support this project by becoming a [sponsor](https://seanmonstar.com/sponsor).

# rustls - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustls/^0.23/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#rustls---a-modern-tls-library)Rustls - a modern TLS library

Rustls is a TLS library that aims to provide a good level of cryptographic security, requires no configuration to achieve that security, and provides no unsafe features or obsolete cryptography by default.

Rustls implements TLS1.2 and TLS1.3 for both clients and servers. See [the full
list of protocol features](https://docs.rs/manual/_04_features/index.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#platform-support)Platform support

While Rustls itself is platform independent, by default it uses [ aws-lc-rs](https://crates.io/crates/aws-lc-rs) for implementing
the cryptography in TLS.  See

[the aws-lc-rs FAQ](https://aws.github.io/aws-lc-rs/faq.html#can-i-run-aws-lc-rs-on-x-platform-or-architecture)for more details of the platform/architecture support constraints in aws-lc-rs.

[ ring](https://crates.io/crates/ring) is also available via the

`ring` crate feature: see
[the supported](https://github.com/briansmith/ring/blob/2e8363b433fa3b3962c877d9ed2e9145612f3160/include/ring-core/target.h#L18-L64).

`ring` target platformsBy providing a custom instance of the [ crypto::CryptoProvider](https://docs.rs/crypto/struct.CryptoProvider.html) struct, you
can replace all cryptography dependencies of rustls.  This is a route to being portable
to a wider set of architectures and environments, or compliance requirements.  See the

[documentation for more details.](https://docs.rs/crypto/struct.CryptoProvider.html)

`crypto::CryptoProvider`Specifying `default-features = false` when depending on rustls will remove the implicit
dependency on aws-lc-rs.

Rustls requires Rust 1.71 or later. It has an optional dependency on zlib-rs which requires 1.75 or later.

[§](https://docs.rs#cryptography-providers)Cryptography providers

Since Rustls 0.22 it has been possible to choose the provider of the cryptographic primitives
that Rustls uses. This may be appealing if you have specific platform, compliance or feature
requirements that aren’t met by the default provider, [ aws-lc-rs](https://crates.io/crates/aws-lc-rs).

Users that wish to customize the provider in use can do so when constructing `ClientConfig`
and `ServerConfig` instances using the `with_crypto_provider` method on the respective config
builder types. See the [ crypto::CryptoProvider](https://docs.rs/crypto/struct.CryptoProvider.html) documentation for more details.

[§](https://docs.rs#built-in-providers)Built-in providers

Rustls ships with two built-in providers controlled by associated crate features:

- `aws-lc-rs`- `aws_lc_rs`crate feature enabled.
- `ring`- `ring`crate feature enabled.

See the documentation for [ crypto::CryptoProvider](https://docs.rs/crypto/struct.CryptoProvider.html) for details on how providers are
selected.

[§](https://docs.rs#third-party-providers)Third-party providers

The community has also started developing third-party providers for Rustls:

- `boring-rustls-provider`- `boringssl`
- `rustls-graviola`- `graviola`
- `rustls-mbedtls-provider`- `mbedtls`
- `rustls-openssl`- [OpenSSL](https://openssl-library.org/)for cryptography.
- `rustls-rustcrypto`- `RustCrypto`
- `rustls-symcrypt`- [SymCrypt](https://github.com/microsoft/SymCrypt)library.
- `rustls-wolfcrypt-provider`- `wolfCrypt`

[§](https://docs.rs#custom-provider)Custom provider

We also provide a simple example of writing your own provider in the [custom provider example](https://github.com/rustls/rustls/tree/main/provider-example/).
This example implements a minimal provider using parts of the [ RustCrypto](https://github.com/RustCrypto) ecosystem.

See the [Making a custom CryptoProvider](https://docs.rs/rustls/latest/rustls/crypto/struct.CryptoProvider.html#making-a-custom-cryptoprovider) section of the documentation for more information
on this topic.

[§](https://docs.rs#design-overview)Design overview

Rustls is a low-level library. If your goal is to make HTTPS connections you may prefer
to use a library built on top of Rustls like [hyper](https://crates.io/crates/hyper) or [ureq](https://crates.io/crates/ureq).

[§](https://docs.rs#rustls-does-not-take-care-of-network-io)Rustls does not take care of network IO

It doesn’t make or accept TCP connections, or do DNS, or read or write files.

Our [examples](https://github.com/rustls/rustls/tree/main/examples) directory contains demos that show how to handle I/O using the
[ stream::Stream](https://docs.rs/struct.Stream.html) helper, as well as more complex asynchronous I/O using

[. If you’re already using Tokio for an async runtime you may prefer to use](https://docs.rs/mio/latest/mio/)

`mio`[instead of interacting with rustls directly.](https://github.com/rustls/tokio-rustls)

`tokio-rustls`[§](https://docs.rs#rustls-provides-encrypted-pipes)Rustls provides encrypted pipes

These are the [ ServerConnection](https://docs.rs/server/struct.ServerConnection.html) and

[types. You supply raw TLS traffic on the left (via the](https://docs.rs/client/struct.ClientConnection.html)

`ClientConnection`[and](https://docs.rs/enum.Connection.html#method.read_tls)

`read_tls()`[methods) and then read/write the plaintext on the right:](https://docs.rs/enum.Connection.html#method.read_tls)

`write_tls()````
         TLS                                   Plaintext
         ===                                   =========
    read_tls()      +-----------------------+      reader() as io::Read
                    |                       |
          +--------->   ClientConnection    +--------->
                    |          or           |
          <---------+   ServerConnection    <---------+
                    |                       |
    write_tls()     +-----------------------+      writer() as io::Write
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rustls-takes-care-of-server-certificate-verification)Rustls takes care of server certificate verification

You do not need to provide anything other than a set of root certificates to trust. Certificate verification cannot be turned off or disabled in the main API.

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting started

This is the minimum you need to do to make a TLS client connection.

First we load some root certificates.  These are used to authenticate the server.
The simplest way is to depend on the [ webpki_roots](https://crates.io/crates/webpki-roots) crate which contains
the Mozilla set of root certificates.

```
let root_store = rustls::RootCertStore::from_iter(
    webpki_roots::TLS_SERVER_ROOTS
        .iter()
        .cloned(),
);
```
Next, we make a `ClientConfig`.  You’re likely to make one of these per process,
and use it for all connections made by that process.

```
let config = rustls::ClientConfig::builder()
    .with_root_certificates(root_store)
    .with_no_client_auth();
```
Now we can make a connection. You need to provide the server’s hostname so we know what to expect to find in the server’s certificate.

```
let rc_config = Arc::new(config);
let example_com = "example.com".try_into().unwrap();
let mut client = rustls::ClientConnection::new(rc_config, example_com);
```
Now you should do appropriate IO for the `client` object.  If `client.wants_read()` yields
true, you should call `client.read_tls()` when the underlying connection has data.
Likewise, if `client.wants_write()` yields true, you should call `client.write_tls()`
when the underlying connection is able to send data.  You should continue doing this
as long as the connection is valid.

The return types of `read_tls()` and `write_tls()` only tell you if the IO worked.  No
parsing or processing of the TLS messages is done.  After each `read_tls()` you should
therefore call `client.process_new_packets()` which parses and processes the messages.
Any error returned from `process_new_packets` is fatal to the connection, and will tell you
why.  For example, if the server’s certificate is expired `process_new_packets` will
return `Err(InvalidCertificate(Expired))`.  From this point on,
`process_new_packets` will not do any new work and will return that error continually.

You can extract newly received data by calling `client.reader()` (which implements the
`io::Read` trait).  You can send data to the peer by calling `client.writer()` (which
implements `io::Write` trait).  Note that `client.writer().write()` buffers data you
send if the TLS connection is not yet established: this is useful for writing (say) a
HTTP request, but this is buffered so avoid large amounts of data.

The following code uses a fictional socket IO API for illustration, and does not handle errors.

```
use std::io;
use rustls::Connection;
client.writer().write(b"GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n").unwrap();
let mut socket = connect("example.com", 443);
loop {
  if client.wants_read() && socket.ready_for_read() {
    client.read_tls(&mut socket).unwrap();
    client.process_new_packets().unwrap();
    let mut plaintext = Vec::new();
    client.reader().read_to_end(&mut plaintext).unwrap();
    io::stdout().write(&plaintext).unwrap();
  }
  if client.wants_write() && socket.ready_for_write() {
    client.write_tls(&mut socket).unwrap();
  }
  socket.wait_for_something_to_happen();
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

You can find several client and server examples of varying complexity in the [examples](https://github.com/rustls/rustls/tree/main/examples)
directory, including [ tlsserver-mio](https://github.com/rustls/rustls/blob/main/examples/src/bin/tlsserver-mio.rs)
and

[- full worked examples using](https://github.com/rustls/rustls/blob/main/examples/src/bin/tlsclient-mio.rs)

`tlsclient-mio`[.](https://docs.rs/mio/latest/mio/)

`mio`[§](https://docs.rs#manual)Manual

The [rustls manual](https://docs.rs/manual/index.html) explains design decisions and includes how-to guidance.

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate features

Here’s a list of what features are exposed by the rustls crate and what they mean.

-
`std`(enabled by default): enable the high-level (buffered) Connection API and other functionality which relies on the`std`library.
-
`aws_lc_rs`(enabled by default): makes the rustls crate depend on the`aws-lc-rs``rustls::crypto::aws_lc_rs::default_provider().install_default()`to use it as the default`CryptoProvider`, or provide it explicitly when making a`ClientConfig`or`ServerConfig`.Note that aws-lc-rs has additional build-time dependencies like cmake. See [the documentation](https://aws.github.io/aws-lc-rs/requirements/index.html)for details.
-
`ring`: makes the rustls crate depend on the*ring*crate for cryptography. Use`rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider().install_default()`to use it as the default`CryptoProvider`, or provide it explicitly when making a`ClientConfig`or`ServerConfig`.
-
`fips`: enable support for FIPS140-3-approved cryptography, via the`aws-lc-rs``aws_lc_rs`crate feature, which makes the rustls crate depend on[aws-lc-rs](https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs). It also changes the default for`ServerConfig::require_ems``ClientConfig::require_ems`See [manual::_06_fips](https://docs.rs/manual/_06_fips/index.html)for more details.
-
`prefer-post-quantum`(enabled by default): for the`aws-lc-rs``rustls::crypto::aws_lc_rs::DEFAULT_KX_GROUPS`. See[the manual](https://docs.rs/manual/_05_defaults/index.html#about-the-post-quantum-secure-key-exchange-x25519mlkem768)for more details.
-
`custom-provider`: disables implicit use of built-in providers (`aws-lc-rs`or`ring`). This forces applications to manually install one, for instance, when using a custom`CryptoProvider`.
-
`tls12`(enabled by default): enable support for TLS version 1.2. Note that, due to the additive nature of Cargo features and because it is enabled by default, other crates in your dependency graph could re-enable it for your application. If you want to disable TLS 1.2 for security reasons, consider explicitly enabling TLS 1.3 only in the config builder API.
-
`logging`(enabled by default): make the rustls crate depend on the`log`crate. rustls outputs interesting protocol-level messages at`trace!`and`debug!`level, and protocol-level errors at`warn!`and`error!`level. The log messages do not contain secret key data, and so are safe to archive without affecting session security.
-
`read_buf`: when building with Rust Nightly, adds support for the unstable`std::io::ReadBuf`and related APIs. This reduces costs from initializing buffers. Will do nothing on non-Nightly releases.
-
`brotli`: uses the`brotli`crate for RFC8879 certificate compression support.
-
`zlib`: uses the`zlib-rs`crate for RFC8879 certificate compression support.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Alert](https://docs.rs/enum.AlertDescription.html)- Description
- The `AlertDescription`TLS protocol enum. Values in this enum are taken from the various RFCs covering TLS, and are listed by IANA. The`Unknown`item is used when processing unrecognised ordinals.
- [Cert](https://docs.rs/enum.CertRevocationListError.html)- Revocation - List - Error
- The ways in which a certificate revocation list (CRL) can be invalid.
- [Certificate](https://docs.rs/enum.CertificateCompressionAlgorithm.html)- Compression - Algorithm
- The “TLS Certificate Compression Algorithm IDs” TLS protocol enum.
Values in this enum are taken from [RFC8879](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8879.html#section-7.3).
- [Certificate](https://docs.rs/enum.CertificateError.html)- Error
- The ways in which certificate validators can express errors.
- [Cipher](https://docs.rs/enum.CipherSuite.html)- Suite
- The `CipherSuite`TLS protocol enum. Values in this enum are taken from the various RFCs covering TLS, and are listed by IANA. The`Unknown`item is used when processing unrecognised ordinals.
- [Connection](https://docs.rs/enum.Connection.html)- `std`
- A client or server connection.
- [Connection](https://docs.rs/enum.ConnectionTrafficSecrets.html)- Traffic - Secrets
- Secrets used to encrypt/decrypt data in a TLS session.
- [Content](https://docs.rs/enum.ContentType.html)- Type
- The `ContentType`TLS protocol enum. Values in this enum are taken from the various RFCs covering TLS, and are listed by IANA. The`Unknown`item is used when processing unrecognised ordinals.
- [Encrypted](https://docs.rs/enum.EncryptedClientHelloError.html)- Client - Hello - Error
- An error that occurred while handling Encrypted Client Hello (ECH).
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- rustls reports protocol errors using this type.
- [Extended](https://docs.rs/enum.ExtendedKeyPurpose.html)- KeyPurpose
- Extended Key Usage (EKU) purpose values.
- [Handshake](https://docs.rs/enum.HandshakeKind.html)- Kind
- Describes which sort of handshake happened.
- [Handshake](https://docs.rs/enum.HandshakeType.html)- Type
- The `HandshakeType`TLS protocol enum. Values in this enum are taken from the various RFCs covering TLS, and are listed by IANA. The`Unknown`item is used when processing unrecognised ordinals.
- [Inconsistent](https://docs.rs/enum.InconsistentKeys.html)- Keys
- Specific failure cases from `keys_match``crate::crypto::signer::SigningKey`
- [Invalid](https://docs.rs/enum.InvalidMessage.html)- Message
- A corrupt TLS message payload that resulted in an error.
- [Named](https://docs.rs/enum.NamedGroup.html)- Group
- The `NamedGroup`TLS protocol enum. Values in this enum are taken from the various RFCs covering TLS, and are listed by IANA. The`Unknown`item is used when processing unrecognised ordinals.
- [Peer](https://docs.rs/enum.PeerIncompatible.html)- Incompatible
- The set of cases where we failed to make a connection because a peer doesn’t support a TLS version/feature we require.
- [Peer](https://docs.rs/enum.PeerMisbehaved.html)- Misbehaved
- The set of cases where we failed to make a connection because we thought the peer was misbehaving.
- [Protocol](https://docs.rs/enum.ProtocolVersion.html)- Version
- The `ProtocolVersion`TLS protocol enum. Values in this enum are taken from the various RFCs covering TLS, and are listed by IANA. The`Unknown`item is used when processing unrecognised ordinals.
- [Side](https://docs.rs/enum.Side.html)
- Side of the connection.
- [Signature](https://docs.rs/enum.SignatureAlgorithm.html)- Algorithm
- The `SignatureAlgorithm`TLS protocol enum. Values in this enum are taken from the various RFCs covering TLS, and are listed by IANA. The`Unknown`item is used when processing unrecognised ordinals.
- [Signature](https://docs.rs/enum.SignatureScheme.html)- Scheme
- The `SignatureScheme`TLS protocol enum. Values in this enum are taken from the various RFCs covering TLS, and are listed by IANA. The`Unknown`item is used when processing unrecognised ordinals.
- [Supported](https://docs.rs/enum.SupportedCipherSuite.html)- Cipher - Suite
- A cipher suite supported by rustls.

## Statics[§](https://docs.rs#statics)

- [ALL_](https://docs.rs/static.ALL_VERSIONS.html)- VERSIONS
- A list of all the protocol versions supported by rustls.
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/static.DEFAULT_VERSIONS.html)- VERSIONS
- The version configuration that an application should use by default.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Config](https://docs.rs/trait.ConfigSide.html)- Side
- Helper trait to abstract `ConfigBuilder``ClientConfig``ServerConfig`
- [KeyLog](https://docs.rs/trait.KeyLog.html)
- This trait represents the ability to do something useful with key material, such as logging it to a file for debugging.
- [Side](https://docs.rs/trait.SideData.html)- Data
- Data specific to the peer’s side (client or server).

# sha2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sha2/^0.10/

## Expand description

An implementation of the [SHA-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2) cryptographic hash algorithms.

There are 6 standard algorithms specified in the SHA-2 standard: [ Sha224](https://docs.rs/type.Sha224.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/type.Sha256.html)

`Sha256`[,](https://docs.rs/type.Sha512_224.html)

`Sha512_224`[,](https://docs.rs/type.Sha512_256.html)

`Sha512_256`[, and](https://docs.rs/type.Sha384.html)

`Sha384`[.](https://docs.rs/type.Sha512.html)

`Sha512`Algorithmically, there are only 2 core algorithms: SHA-256 and SHA-512. All other algorithms are just applications of these with different initial hash values, and truncated to different digest bit lengths. The first two algorithms in the list are based on SHA-256, while the last four are based on SHA-512.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#one-shot-api)One-shot API

```
use hex_literal::hex;
use sha2::{Sha256, Digest};
let result = Sha256::digest(b"hello world");
assert_eq!(result[..], hex!("
    b94d27b9934d3e08a52e52d7da7dabfac484efe37a5380ee9088f7ace2efcde9
")[..]);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#incremental-api)Incremental API

```
use hex_literal::hex;
use sha2::{Sha256, Sha512, Digest};
// create a Sha256 object
let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
// write input message
hasher.update(b"hello world");
// read hash digest and consume hasher
let result = hasher.finalize();
assert_eq!(result[..], hex!("
    b94d27b9934d3e08a52e52d7da7dabfac484efe37a5380ee9088f7ace2efcde9
")[..]);
// same for Sha512
let mut hasher = Sha512::new();
hasher.update(b"hello world");
let result = hasher.finalize();
assert_eq!(result[..], hex!("
    309ecc489c12d6eb4cc40f50c902f2b4d0ed77ee511a7c7a9bcd3ca86d4cd86f
    989dd35bc5ff499670da34255b45b0cfd830e81f605dcf7dc5542e93ae9cd76f
")[..]);
```
Also see [RustCrypto/hashes](https://github.com/RustCrypto/hashes) readme.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [digest](https://docs.rs/digest/0.10.7/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/digest/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Sha256](https://docs.rs/struct.Sha256VarCore.html)- VarCore
- Core block-level SHA-256 hasher with variable output size.
- [Sha512](https://docs.rs/struct.Sha512VarCore.html)- VarCore
- Core block-level SHA-512 hasher with variable output size.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Digest](https://docs.rs/trait.Digest.html)
- Convenience wrapper trait covering functionality of cryptographic hash functions with fixed output size.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [compress256](https://docs.rs/fn.compress256.html)- `compress`
- Raw SHA-256 compression function.
- [compress512](https://docs.rs/fn.compress512.html)- `compress`
- Raw SHA-512 compression function.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Sha224](https://docs.rs/type.Sha224.html)
- SHA-224 hasher.
- [Sha256](https://docs.rs/type.Sha256.html)
- SHA-256 hasher.
- [Sha384](https://docs.rs/type.Sha384.html)
- SHA-384 hasher.
- [Sha512](https://docs.rs/type.Sha512.html)
- SHA-512 hasher.
