# thiserror - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/thiserror/^2/

## Expand description

This library provides a convenient derive macro for the standard library’s
[ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/error/trait.Error.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use thiserror::Error;
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum DataStoreError {
    #[error("data store disconnected")]
    Disconnect(#[from] io::Error),
    #[error("the data for key `{0}` is not available")]
    Redaction(String),
    #[error("invalid header (expected {expected:?}, found {found:?})")]
    InvalidHeader {
        expected: String,
        found: String,
    },
    #[error("unknown data store error")]
    Unknown,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Thiserror deliberately does not appear in your public API. You get the same thing as if you had written an implementation of `std::error::Error`
-
Errors may be enums, structs with named fields, tuple structs, or unit structs.
-
A `Display``#[error("...")]`messages on the struct or each variant of your enum, as shown above in the example.The messages support a shorthand for interpolating fields from the error. - `#[error("{var}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.0)`
- `#[error("{var:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.0)`
 These shorthands can be used together with any additional format args, which may be arbitrary expressions. For example: `#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("invalid rdo_lookahead_frames {0} (expected < {max})", max = i32::MAX)] InvalidLookahead(u32), }`If one of the additional expression arguments needs to refer to a field of the struct or enum, then refer to named fields as `.var`and tuple fields as`.0`.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("first letter must be lowercase but was {:?}", first_char(.0))] WrongCase(String), #[error("invalid index {idx}, expected at least {} and at most {}", .limits.lo, .limits.hi)] OutOfBounds { idx: usize, limits: Limits }, }`
-
A `From``#[from]`attribute.The variant using `#[from]`must not contain any other fields beyond the source error (and possibly a backtrace — see below). Usually`#[from]`fields are unnamed, but`#[from]`is allowed on a named field too.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io(#[from] io::Error), Glob(#[from] globset::Error), }`
-
The Error trait’s `source()``#[source]`attribute or is named`source`, if any. This is for identifying the underlying lower level error that caused your error.The `#[from]`attribute always implies that the same field is`#[source]`, so you don’t ever need to specify both attributes.Any error type that implements `std::error::Error`or dereferences to`dyn std::error::Error`will work as a source.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, #[source] // optional if field name is `source` source: anyhow::Error, }`
-
The Error trait’s `provide()``Backtrace`, if any, as a`std::backtrace::Backtrace``Backtrace`in errors requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`use std::backtrace::Backtrace; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, backtrace: Backtrace, // automatically detected }`
-
If a field is both a source (named `source`, or has`#[source]`or`#[from]`attribute)*and*is marked`#[backtrace]`, then the Error trait’s`provide()``provide`so that both layers of the error share the same backtrace. The`#[backtrace]`attribute requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[backtrace] source: io::Error, }, }`
-
For variants that use `#[from]`and also contain a`Backtrace`field, a backtrace is captured from within the`From`impl.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[from] source: io::Error, backtrace: Backtrace, }, }`
-
Errors may use `error(transparent)`to forward the source and`Display``#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { ... #[error(transparent)] Other(#[from] anyhow::Error), // source and Display delegate to anyhow::Error }`Another use case is hiding implementation details of an error representation behind an opaque error type, so that the representation is able to evolve without breaking the crate’s public API. `// PublicError is public, but opaque and easy to keep compatible. #[derive(Error, Debug)] #[error(transparent)] pub struct PublicError(#[from] ErrorRepr); impl PublicError { // Accessors for anything we do want to expose publicly. } // Private and free to change across minor version of the crate. #[derive(Error, Debug)] enum ErrorRepr { ... }`
-
See also the `anyhow`

---

# fakecloud_k8s - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fakecloud-k8s/0.31.0/target-redirect/fakecloud_k8s/

## Expand description

Shared Kubernetes-backend primitives for FakeCloud.

FakeCloud can run its container-backed services (Lambda, ElastiCache,
RDS, ECS) either by shelling out to a local Docker/Podman daemon (the
default) or by spawning native Pods in a Kubernetes cluster. The k8s
path is the same for every service — connect a client, build a Pod,
wait for it to come up, optionally `exec` into it, tear it down, and
reap orphans left by a previous process. This crate holds that common
machinery so each service only has to describe *its* Pod, not
re-implement the client bootstrap, readiness polling, exec plumbing,
reaping, and DNS-safe naming.

Backend selection (`FAKECLOUD_CONTAINER_BACKEND` /
`FAKECLOUD_<SERVICE>_BACKEND`) lives in [ backend](https://docs.rs/backend/index.html). The kube client
wrapper and Pod lifecycle live in

[. Env parsing (](https://docs.rs/client/index.html)

`client``FAKECLOUD_K8S_*`) lives in [`env`]. Operator-configurable Pod
scheduling/metadata (node selector, tolerations, annotations) lives in
[. Naming + label conventions live in](https://docs.rs/pod_config/index.html)

`pod_config`[and](https://docs.rs/names/index.html)

`names`[.](https://docs.rs/labels/index.html)

`labels`See `website/content/docs/guides/kubernetes-backend.md` for the
operator-facing setup (ServiceAccount, RBAC, Deployment yaml).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use backend::`- [backend_choice](https://docs.rs/backend/fn.backend_choice.html);
- `pub use backend::`- [Backend](https://docs.rs/backend/enum.Backend.html);
- `pub use client::`- [ExecOutput](https://docs.rs/client/struct.ExecOutput.html);
- `pub use client::`- [K8sClient](https://docs.rs/client/struct.K8sClient.html);
- `pub use client::`- [K8sError](https://docs.rs/client/enum.K8sError.html);
- `pub use env::`- [K8sEnv](https://docs.rs/env/struct.K8sEnv.html);
- `pub use env::`- [K8sEnvError](https://docs.rs/env/enum.K8sEnvError.html);
- `pub use pod_config::`- [K8sPodConfig](https://docs.rs/pod_config/struct.K8sPodConfig.html);
- `pub use pod_config::`- [K8sPodConfigError](https://docs.rs/pod_config/enum.K8sPodConfigError.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [backend](https://docs.rs/backend/index.html)
- Backend selection: Docker (default) vs native Kubernetes Pods.
- [client](https://docs.rs/client/index.html)
- Kube client wrapper + generic Pod lifecycle shared by every backend.
- [env](https://docs.rs/env/index.html)
- Parsing of the `FAKECLOUD_K8S_*`operator configuration.

- Operator-configurable Pod scheduling + metadata shared by every FakeCloud k8s backend.

# fakecloud_k8s::backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fakecloud-k8s/0.31.0/fakecloud_k8s/backend/index.html

## Expand description

Backend selection: Docker (default) vs native Kubernetes Pods.

A FakeCloud server can run every container-backed service on Docker (the default) or on Kubernetes. The choice is per-service with a global fallback:

- `FAKECLOUD_<SERVICE>_BACKEND=k8s|docker`— explicit per-service override (e.g.- `FAKECLOUD_ELASTICACHE_BACKEND`,- `FAKECLOUD_LAMBDA_BACKEND`). An explicit value always wins.
- `FAKECLOUD_CONTAINER_BACKEND=k8s|docker`— global default applied to any service whose own variable is unset.
- Unset everywhere -> `Backend::Docker`

This lets an operator flip the whole stack to Kubernetes with one variable while still pinning an individual service back to Docker.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Backend](https://docs.rs/enum.Backend.html)
- Which execution backend a service should use.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [GLOBAL_](https://docs.rs/constant.GLOBAL_BACKEND_ENV.html)- BACKEND_ - ENV
- The global default backend variable, consulted when a service’s own variable is unset.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [backend_](https://docs.rs/fn.backend_choice.html)- choice
- Resolve the backend for a service given the name of its per-service
override variable (e.g. `"FAKECLOUD_ELASTICACHE_BACKEND"`).

---

# fakecloud_k8s::client - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fakecloud-k8s/0.31.0/fakecloud_k8s/client/index.html

## Expand description

Kube client wrapper + generic Pod lifecycle shared by every backend.

Wraps a [ kube::Client](https://docs.rs/kube-client/0.95.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kube_client/client/struct.Client.html) scoped to one namespace and provides the
handful of operations every FakeCloud k8s backend performs: create a
Pod (idempotently, replacing any stale same-named Pod), wait for it
to get an IP and become reachable,

`exec` a command inside it, delete
it, and reap Pods orphaned by a previous process. Service-specific
Pod *construction*stays in each service; this is only the plumbing.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Exec](https://docs.rs/struct.ExecOutput.html)- Output
- Output of an `K8sClient::exec`
- [K8sClient](https://docs.rs/struct.K8sClient.html)
- A namespaced kube client plus this process’s instance identity.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [K8sError](https://docs.rs/enum.K8sError.html)
- Errors from Pod lifecycle operations.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [ensure_](https://docs.rs/fn.ensure_crypto_provider.html)- crypto_ - provider
- Install rustls’ `ring`CryptoProvider once per process. Rustls 0.23 dropped the implicit default and every TLS connection panics until one is installed; kube’s`rustls-tls`feature doesn’t pull one in on our behalf. Safe to call concurrently and repeatedly — the`.ok()`swallows the “already installed” error.

---

# fakecloud_k8s::pod_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fakecloud-k8s/0.31.0/fakecloud_k8s/pod_config/index.html

## Expand description

Operator-configurable Pod scheduling + metadata shared by every FakeCloud k8s backend.

Lets operators attach a `nodeSelector`, taint `tolerations`, and
arbitrary `annotations` to the Pods FakeCloud creates, without each
service re-implementing the parsing and application. Each of the three
is resolvable at three levels, lowest to highest precedence:

- Global env  - `FAKECLOUD_K8S_<KEY>`
- Service env - `FAKECLOUD_<SERVICE>_K8S_<KEY>`(e.g.`FAKECLOUD_LAMBDA_K8S_NODE_SELECTOR`)
- Per-instance tag - a reserved tag on the resource itself
(e.g. a Lambda function tag `fakecloud-k8s/node-selector`)

A backend reads the global+service base once at startup with
[ K8sPodConfig::resolved_base](https://docs.rs/struct.K8sPodConfig.html#method.resolved_base), then per-Pod merges the resource’s
tags over it with

[+](https://docs.rs/struct.K8sPodConfig.html#method.merge)

`K8sPodConfig::merge`[and writes the result onto the built Pod with](https://docs.rs/struct.K8sPodConfig.html#method.from_tags)

`K8sPodConfig::from_tags`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.K8sPodConfig.html#method.apply)

`K8sPodConfig::apply`Value formats:

- `NODE_SELECTOR`/- `ANNOTATIONS`: a flat- `key=value,key=value`map.
- `TOLERATIONS`: a JSON array of k8s- `Toleration`objects.

Merge semantics across the three levels: the maps (node selector, annotations) union per key, with the higher level winning on a key clash; tolerations combine additively (a Pod tolerates the union of taints), dropping exact duplicates. This mirrors the repo’s SAM Globals convention (maps deep-merge, list-typed keys combine).

Error handling is asymmetric on purpose: a malformed *env* value fails
fast at startup (an operator typo should be loud), but a malformed
per-instance *tag* is warned about and ignored for that field – a bad
tag must never make a single resource un-runnable.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [K8sPod](https://docs.rs/struct.K8sPodConfig.html)- Config
- Resolved node selector, tolerations, and annotations for a Pod.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [K8sPod](https://docs.rs/enum.K8sPodConfigError.html)- Config - Error
- Errors parsing the `FAKECLOUD_*_K8S_*`Pod configuration. Only env parsing fails fast; per-instance tags warn and fall back instead.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [TAG_](https://docs.rs/constant.TAG_ANNOTATIONS.html)- ANNOTATIONS
- Reserved per-instance tag key carrying `key=value,key=value`annotations merged onto this resource’s Pod.
- [TAG_](https://docs.rs/constant.TAG_NODE_SELECTOR.html)- NODE_ - SELECTOR
- Reserved per-instance tag key carrying a `key=value,key=value`node-selector for this resource’s Pod.
- [TAG_](https://docs.rs/constant.TAG_TOLERATIONS.html)- TOLERATIONS
- Reserved per-instance tag key carrying a JSON array of `Toleration`s.

# fakecloud_k8s::names - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fakecloud-k8s/0.31.0/fakecloud_k8s/names/index.html

## Expand description

DNS-1123-safe naming helpers shared by every FakeCloud k8s backend.

Kubernetes object names must be DNS-1123 labels: lowercase
alphanumerics and dashes, 63 chars max, ending in an alphanumeric.
Resource identifiers FakeCloud works with (function names, cluster
IDs, task ARNs) routinely violate that, so every backend funnels its
identifiers through [ pod_name](https://docs.rs/fn.pod_name.html) /

[.](https://docs.rs/fn.label_safe.html)

`label_safe`## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DNS1123_](https://docs.rs/constant.DNS1123_MAX.html)- MAX
- Maximum length of a DNS-1123 label (and therefore a Pod name).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [label_](https://docs.rs/fn.label_safe.html)- safe
- Lowercase + replace anything outside `[a-z0-9-]`with`-`, then trim leading and trailing dashes so the result both starts and ends in an alphanumeric (DNS-1123 label requirements — a leading dash is just as invalid as a trailing one). Does not enforce the length cap — callers that need a bounded label should truncate the result.
- [pod_](https://docs.rs/fn.pod_name.html)- name
- Build a deterministic, DNS-1123-safe Pod name of the form
`<prefix>-<id-part>-<hex12>`.
- [simple_](https://docs.rs/fn.simple_hex12.html)- hex12
- 12-char hex projection of an arbitrary string. Used to suffix Pod names so that a changed identifier (a new deploy, a recreated resource) produces a fresh, non-colliding Pod name while staying deterministic — the launcher and any later lookup agree on the name. Not cryptographic; the 2^48 space is ample for per-resource uniqueness within a namespace.

---

# fakecloud_k8s::labels - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fakecloud-k8s/0.31.0/fakecloud_k8s/labels/index.html

## Expand description

Pod label conventions shared by every FakeCloud k8s backend.

Every Pod FakeCloud creates carries three labels so it can be found and cleaned up later:

- `MANAGED_BY`- `MANAGED_BY_VALUE`
- `INSTANCE`- `fakecloud-<pid>`), so a restarted server can tell its own Pods from a dead run’s.
- `SERVICE`- `lambda`,- `elasticache`,- `rds`,- `ecs`) so each service reaps only its own kind of Pod.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [INSTANCE](https://docs.rs/constant.INSTANCE.html)
- Label key holding the owning process identity (`fakecloud-<pid>`).
- [MANAGED_](https://docs.rs/constant.MANAGED_BY.html)- BY
- Label key marking a Pod as managed by FakeCloud.
- [MANAGED_](https://docs.rs/constant.MANAGED_BY_VALUE.html)- BY_ - VALUE
- Value for `MANAGED_BY`
- [SERVICE](https://docs.rs/constant.SERVICE.html)
- Label key holding the owning service name.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [instance_](https://docs.rs/fn.instance_id.html)- id
- The per-process instance identity used for the `INSTANCE`

---

# backend_choice in fakecloud_k8s::backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fakecloud-k8s/0.31.0/fakecloud_k8s/backend/fn.backend_choice.html

## Expand description

Resolve the backend for a service given the name of its per-service
override variable (e.g. `"FAKECLOUD_ELASTICACHE_BACKEND"`).

An explicit per-service value wins over the global default; only
`k8s` and `docker` are recognized (case-insensitive), and any other
value is ignored (treated as unset) so a typo can’t silently leave a
service on an unexpected backend without falling through to the
documented precedence.

---

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fakecloud_k8s/client.rs.html#445-459)#### pub async fn [cni_component_names](https://docs.rs#method.cni_component_names)(&self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fakecloud_k8s/client.rs.html#445-459)

#### pub async fn [cni_component_names](https://docs.rs#method.cni_component_names)(&self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

Best-effort detection of the cluster CNI from Pod names across the
namespaces CNIs commonly install into (e.g. `calico-node-*`, `cilium-*`,
`kindnet-*`). Returns the matched component names; the caller maps them
to a driver. An empty result (lists failed or no recognizable CNI) maps
to “unknown”.

Scans `kube-system` plus the operator namespaces Calico/Cilium use
(`calico-system`, `tigera-operator`, `cilium`) so a Tigera-operator or
dedicated-namespace install isn’t mis-reported as non-enforcing
(bug-hunt 2026-06-18 finding 1.6). Per-namespace list errors (RBAC /
absent namespace) are swallowed.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fakecloud_k8s/pod_config.rs.html#76-94)#### pub fn [from_env_prefix](https://docs.rs#method.from_env_prefix)(prefix: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [K8sPodConfigError](https://docs.rs/enum.K8sPodConfigError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fakecloud_k8s/pod_config.rs.html#76-94)

#### pub fn [from_env_prefix](https://docs.rs#method.from_env_prefix)(prefix: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [K8sPodConfigError](https://docs.rs/enum.K8sPodConfigError.html)>

Read a single env level. `prefix` is the part before the key, e.g.
`FAKECLOUD_K8S` (global) or `FAKECLOUD_LAMBDA_K8S` (service). Reads
`{prefix}_NODE_SELECTOR`, `{prefix}_TOLERATIONS`, and
`{prefix}_ANNOTATIONS`. Empty/whitespace values are treated as
unset; malformed tolerations JSON fails fast.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fakecloud_k8s/pod_config.rs.html#100-104)#### pub fn [resolved_base](https://docs.rs#method.resolved_base)(service_prefix: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [K8sPodConfigError](https://docs.rs/enum.K8sPodConfigError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fakecloud_k8s/pod_config.rs.html#100-104)

#### pub fn [resolved_base](https://docs.rs#method.resolved_base)(service_prefix: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [K8sPodConfigError](https://docs.rs/enum.K8sPodConfigError.html)>

The global+service base for a backend: the global
`FAKECLOUD_K8S_*` config with the per-service
`{service_prefix}_*` config merged over it. Call once at backend
startup and keep the result; merge per-instance tags over it later.

Build a config from a resource’s reserved tags. Malformed tolerations are warned about and dropped (a bad tag must not make the resource un-runnable); the other fields still parse.

Merge `higher` (higher precedence) over `self`. Map keys from
`higher` win on a clash; tolerations combine additively, dropping
exact duplicates.

Write this config onto an already-built Pod: merge the node
selector and tolerations into `spec` and the annotations into
`metadata`. Existing entries are preserved (annotation keys this
config sets win; tolerations are added without duplicating). Safe
when `spec` is `None` – node selector/tolerations are simply
skipped, annotations still land on the metadata.

# fakecloud_k8s::env - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fakecloud-k8s/0.31.0/fakecloud_k8s/env/index.html

## Expand description

Parsing of the `FAKECLOUD_K8S_*` operator configuration.

When FakeCloud runs on Kubernetes it needs to know how Pods reach it
back (`FAKECLOUD_K8S_SELF_URL`), which namespace to create Pods in
(`FAKECLOUD_K8S_NAMESPACE`), where its in-cluster ECR endpoint lives
(`FAKECLOUD_K8S_ECR_URL`), and optionally an `imagePullSecrets` name
for private images (`FAKECLOUD_K8S_PULL_SECRET`). Every k8s backend
shares this configuration, so it’s parsed once here.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [K8sEnv](https://docs.rs/struct.K8sEnv.html)
- Parsed `FAKECLOUD_K8S_*`configuration.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [K8sEnv](https://docs.rs/enum.K8sEnvError.html)- Error
- Errors parsing the `FAKECLOUD_K8S_*`configuration.

# guise-ui 0.4.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/guise-ui/0.4.1

# guise

A [Mantine](https://mantine.dev)-inspired component library for
[gpui](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed) — the GPU-accelerated Rust UI
framework that powers Zed.

`guise` brings Mantine's ergonomics to gpui: a themed palette, sizing tokens,
and composable components built on gpui's `RenderOnce` builder pattern.

```
use *;
new
    .gap
    .child
    .child
```
## Documentation

Full docs live in [ docs/](https://docs.rs/docs/readme.md):

- [Getting started](https://docs.rs/docs/gettingstarted.md)·- [Theming](https://docs.rs/docs/theming.md)·- [Component model](https://docs.rs/docs/components.md)
- Components: [Buttons](https://docs.rs/docs/buttons.md)·[Icons](https://docs.rs/docs/icons.md)·[Inputs](https://docs.rs/docs/inputs.md)·[Typography](https://docs.rs/docs/typography.md)·[Layout](https://docs.rs/docs/layout.md)·[Feedback](https://docs.rs/docs/feedback.md)·[Data](https://docs.rs/docs/data.md)·[Overlays](https://docs.rs/docs/overlays.md)·[Navigation](https://docs.rs/docs/navigation.md)
- Systems: [Flex layout](https://docs.rs/docs/flex.md)·[Macros](https://docs.rs/docs/macros.md)·[Transitions](https://docs.rs/docs/transitions.md)·[Reactive state](https://docs.rs/docs/reactive.md)·[Window menu](https://docs.rs/docs/windowmenu.md)·[Architecture](https://docs.rs/docs/architecture.md)

## Workspace

- `crates/guise`
- `crates/gallery`- `cargo run -p gallery`.

## Theme

Install a theme once at startup; every component reads it from the gpui global:

```
dark.init;   // or Theme::light()
```
The theme carries the full Mantine / open-color palette (14 colors × 10 shades),
`xs..xl` scales for spacing, radius and font size, and scheme-aware semantic
colors (`body`, `surface`, `text`, `dimmed`, `border`).

### CSS-style colors

Write colors the CSS way — hex, `rgb`/`rgba`, `hsl`/`hsla`, or named — with the
`color!` macro (compile-time) or `css(..)` (runtime strings). Both produce a
gpui `Hsla`, usable in `.bg(..)`/`.text_color(..)`, in any component `.color(..)`,
and in the theme `with_*` overrides:

```
new.color
new.color
dark
    .with_primary
    .with_body
    .with_text
    .init;                                   // restyles the whole UI
```
`color!` takes `rgb(..)`/`rgba(..)`/`hsl(..)`/`hsla(..)`/named tokens or a CSS
string (hex must be a string — `#228be6` isn't a Rust token). Component
`.color(..)` accepts a palette `ColorName` *or* an explicit color (the
`ColorValue` type) and derives variant shades from a single custom color. See
[Theming](https://docs.rs/docs/theming.md).

## Components

| Group | Components |
|---|---|
| Layout | `Stack`,`Group`,`Center`,`SimpleGrid`,`ScrollArea` |
| Surface | `Paper`,`Card` |
| Typography | `Text`,`Title` |
| Inputs | `Button`,`TextInput`,`TextArea`,`NumberInput`,`Checkbox`,`Switch`,`Radio`,`RadioGroup`,`CheckboxGroup`,`Select`,`Combobox`,`Slider`,`Field` |
| Overlays | `Modal`,`Drawer`,`Menu`,`Popover`,`Spotlight`,`Tooltip` |
| Feedback | `Alert`,`Loader`,`Progress`,`RingProgress`,`Notification`,`ToastStack` |
| Data | `Badge`,`Divider`,`Avatar`,`AvatarGroup`,`List`,`Table`,`Timeline`,`Tabs`,`Accordion` |
| Navigation | `Breadcrumbs`,`NavLink`,`Stepper`,`Pagination`,`StatusBar` |
| Polish | `Icon`,`ActionIcon`,`ThemeIcon`,`CloseButton`,`CopyButton`,`Anchor`,`Code`,`Kbd`,`Chip`,`Indicator`,`Skeleton`,`SegmentedControl` |
| Motion | `Transition`,`Collapse` |

Inputs come in two flavors that match how each control behaves in gpui:

- **Controlled**(- `Checkbox`,- `Switch`,- `Radio`, and the- `RadioGroup`/- `CheckboxGroup`wrappers) are- `RenderOnce`builders — the parent view owns the value and passes a change handler via- `cx.listener(...)`.
- **Stateful**(- `TextInput`,- `TextArea`,- `NumberInput`,- `Select`,- `Combobox`,- `Slider`) are gpui entities that own their buffer / selection. Create with- `cx.new(...)`and subscribe to their events.- `Field`is the shared label/description/error chrome these compose.

Overlays paint above the page (a `deferred` layer): `Modal` and `Drawer` are
controlled backdrops (render while `opened`, pass `on_close`), `Menu` is a
keyboard-navigable trigger + deferred action list, `Popover` is the reusable
anchored-floating primitive, `Spotlight` is a command palette, and `Tooltip`
plugs into gpui's built-in `.tooltip(...)` via the `tooltip(...)` helper.

Feedback components communicate state: `Alert` (inline callout), `Loader`
(animated pulsing dots/bars), `Progress` / `RingProgress` (determinate bar and
circular gauge), `Notification` (an elevated toast card), and `ToastStack` (a
positioned, stacking toast manager).

Data display: `Avatar`, `List`, `Table`, and `Timeline` are stateless builders;
`Tabs` and `Accordion` are stateful entities whose panel content is a builder
closure (`|window, app| ...`) re-invoked each frame so panels can show live data.

Navigation: `Breadcrumbs`, `NavLink`, and `Stepper` are stateless builders;
`Pagination` is a stateful entity (windowed page list with ellipses);
`StatusBar` is a themed app shell with left/center/right slots. The gallery also
wires a **native window menu** (`cx.set_menus`) whose actions toggle the theme
and quit.

## Flex layout (`guise::flex`)

A Flutter-flavored layout kit on top of gpui's flexbox: `Row`, `Column`,
`Container`, `Padding`, `Align`, `Center`, `Expanded`/`Flexible` (real flex
weights), `Spacer`, `SizedBox`, `Stack`/`Positioned`, and `Wrap`, with
`MainAxisAlignment` / `CrossAxisAlignment` / `EdgeInsets`. It is **not**
glob-exported (names overlap with `guise::layout`); import it as
`use guise::flex::*`.

## Layout macros

Terse builders, available from the prelude:

```
col!
```
`row!`/`col!`/`zstack!`/`wrap!` build `flex` containers; `vstack!`/`hstack!`
build the themed `layout::Stack`/`Group`. (It's `col!`, not `column!`, to avoid
the std `column!` macro.)

There's also a CSS-like `style!` block for inline styling, applied with `.apply`:

```
div.apply
```
Numbers are pixels; colors take a CSS string or any `color!`/`Hsla`. See
[Macros](https://docs.rs/docs/macros.md#style--css-like-style-blocks).

## Reactive state (`guise::reactive`)

A small React-flavored layer over gpui's reactivity:

```
// Create state and provide it (React's useState + Context.Provider).
let count = use_state;
provide;
// In a descendant view's constructor: read it back and subscribe.
let count = .unwrap;
watch;          // re-render this view when it changes
// Anywhere with app/context access:
count.update;   // notifies every watcher
```
- `Signal<T>`
- `provide`/- `use_context`
- `use_state`/- `watch`
- `use_form`/- `FormState`- `required`/- `min_len`/- `email`validators.

## Transitions

Mount animations on gpui's animation API: `Transition` plays a one-shot
fade/slide as its child appears (`TransitionKind::Fade | SlideUp | SlideDown | SlideLeft | SlideRight`), and `Collapse` reveals gated content with a fade.

```
new.kind.child
new.open.child
```
## Variants

Colored components share Mantine's variant system: `Filled`, `Light`,
`Outline`, `Subtle`, `Default`, `Transparent`, `White`.

## Installation

```
```
or in `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.2"
 = "0.2"
```
The crate is published on crates.io as

(the`guise-ui``guise`name was taken), but its library is named`guise`— so you still write`use guise::prelude::*;`.

`guise` tracks the published `gpui``0.2`
release on crates.io.

## Building

Requires Rust stable.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE).

# guise-ui 0.4.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/guise-ui/0.4.1/source/

#
                    guise-ui 0.4.1

                A Mantine-inspired component library for gpui, Zed's GPU-accelerated UI framework.

# gpui - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gpui/^0.2.2/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#welcome-to-gpui)Welcome to GPUI!

GPUI is a hybrid immediate and retained mode, GPU accelerated, UI framework for Rust, designed to support a wide variety of applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting Started

GPUI is still in active development as we work on the Zed code editor, and is still pre-1.0. There will often be breaking changes between versions. You’ll also need to use the latest version of stable Rust and be on macOS or Linux. Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

`gpui = { version = "*" }`Everything in GPUI starts with an `Application`. You can create one with `Application::new()`, and kick off your application by passing a callback to `Application::run()`. Inside this callback, you can create a new window with `App::open_window()`, and register your first root view. See [gpui.rs](https://www.gpui.rs/) for a complete example.

[§](https://docs.rs#dependencies)Dependencies

GPUI has various system dependencies that it needs in order to work.

[§](https://docs.rs#macos)macOS

On macOS, GPUI uses Metal for rendering. In order to use Metal, you need to do the following:

- Install [Xcode](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/xcode/id497799835?mt=12)from the macOS App Store, or from the[Apple Developer](https://developer.apple.com/download/all/)website. Note this requires a developer account.

Ensure you launch Xcode after installing, and install the macOS components, which is the default option.

-
Install [Xcode command line tools](https://developer.apple.com/xcode/resources/)`xcode-select --install`
-
Ensure that the Xcode command line tools are using your newly installed copy of Xcode: `sudo xcode-select --switch /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`

[§](https://docs.rs#the-big-picture)The Big Picture

GPUI offers three different [registers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Register_(sociolinguistics)) depending on your needs:

-
State management and communication with `Entity`’s. Whenever you need to store application state that communicates between different parts of your application, you’ll want to use GPUI’s entities. Entities are owned by GPUI and are only accessible through an owned smart pointer similar to an`Rc`. See the`app::context`module for more information.
-
High level, declarative UI with views. All UI in GPUI starts with a view. A view is simply an `Entity`that can be rendered, by implementing the`Render`trait. At the start of each frame, GPUI will call this render method on the root view of a given window. Views build a tree of`elements`, lay them out and style them with a tailwind-style API, and then give them to GPUI to turn into pixels. See the`div`element for an all purpose swiss-army knife of rendering.
-
Low level, imperative UI with Elements. Elements are the building blocks of UI in GPUI, and they provide a nice wrapper around an imperative API that provides as much flexibility and control as you need. Elements have total control over how they and their child elements are rendered and can be used for making efficient views into large lists, implement custom layouting for a code editor, and anything else you can think of. See the `element`module for more information.

Each of these registers has one or more corresponding contexts that can be accessed from all GPUI services. This context is your main interface to GPUI, and is used extensively throughout the framework.

[§](https://docs.rs#other-resources)Other Resources

In addition to the systems above, GPUI provides a range of smaller services that are useful for building complex applications:

-
Actions are user-defined structs that are used for converting keystrokes into logical operations in your UI. Use this for implementing keyboard shortcuts, such as cmd-q. See the `action`module for more information.
-
Platform services, such as `quit the app`or`open a URL`are available as methods on the`app::App`.
-
An async executor that is integrated with the platform’s event loop. See the `executor`module for more information.,
-
The `[gpui::test]`macro provides a convenient way to write tests for your GPUI applications. Tests also have their own kind of context, a`TestAppContext`which provides ways of simulating common platform input. See`app::test_context`and`test`modules for more details.

Currently, the best way to learn about these APIs is to read the Zed source code, ask us about it at a fireside hack, or drop a question in the [Zed Discord](https://zed.dev/community-links). We’re working on improving the documentation, creating more examples, and will be publishing more guides to GPUI on our [blog](https://zed.dev/blog).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [http_client](https://docs.rs/gpui_http_client/0.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gpui_http_client/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [_ownership_](https://docs.rs/_ownership_and_data_flow/index.html)- and_ - data_ - flow
- In GPUI, every model or view in the application is actually owned by a single top-level object called the `App`. When a new entity or view is created (referred to collectively as*entities*), the application is given ownership of their state to enable their participation in a variety of app services and interaction with other entities.
- [colors](https://docs.rs/colors/index.html)
- The default colors used by GPUI.
- [inspector_](https://docs.rs/inspector_reflection/index.html)- reflection
- Provides definitions used by `#[derive_inspector_reflection]`.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- The GPUI prelude is a collection of traits and types that are widely used throughout the library. It is recommended to import this prelude into your application to avoid having to import each trait individually.
- [styled_](https://docs.rs/styled_reflection/index.html)- reflection
- Implements function reflection

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [actions](https://docs.rs/macro.actions.html)
- Defines and registers unit structs that can be used as actions. For more complex data types, derive `Action`.
- [border_](https://docs.rs/macro.border_style_methods.html)- style_ - methods
- Generates methods for border styles.
- [box_](https://docs.rs/macro.box_shadow_style_methods.html)- shadow_ - style_ - methods
- Generates methods for box shadow styles.
- [cursor_](https://docs.rs/macro.cursor_style_methods.html)- style_ - methods
- Generates methods for cursor styles.
- [margin_](https://docs.rs/macro.margin_style_methods.html)- style_ - methods
- Generates methods for margin styles.
- [overflow_](https://docs.rs/macro.overflow_style_methods.html)- style_ - methods
- Generates methods for overflow styles.
- [padding_](https://docs.rs/macro.padding_style_methods.html)- style_ - methods
- Generates methods for padding styles.
- [position_](https://docs.rs/macro.position_style_methods.html)- style_ - methods
- Generates methods for position styles.
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_action.html)- action
- This can be used to register an action with the GPUI runtime when you want to manually implement
the `Action`trait. Typically you should use the`Action`derive macro or`actions!`macro instead.
- [visibility_](https://docs.rs/macro.visibility_style_methods.html)- style_ - methods
- Generates methods for visibility styles.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Anchored](https://docs.rs/struct.Anchored.html)
- An anchored element that can be used to display UI that will avoid overflowing the window bounds.
- [Anchored](https://docs.rs/struct.AnchoredState.html)- State
- The state that the anchored element element uses to track its children.
- [Animation](https://docs.rs/struct.Animation.html)
- An animation that can be applied to an element.
- [Animation](https://docs.rs/struct.AnimationElement.html)- Element
- A GPUI element that applies an animation to another element
- [AnyDrag](https://docs.rs/struct.AnyDrag.html)
- Contains state associated with an active drag operation, started by dragging an element within the window or by dragging into the app from the underlying platform.
- [AnyElement](https://docs.rs/struct.AnyElement.html)
- A dynamically typed element that can be used to store any element type.
- [AnyEntity](https://docs.rs/struct.AnyEntity.html)
- A dynamically typed reference to a entity, which can be downcast into a `Entity<T>`.
- [AnyImage](https://docs.rs/struct.AnyImageCache.html)- Cache
- A dynamically typed image cache, which can be used to store any image cache
- [AnyTooltip](https://docs.rs/struct.AnyTooltip.html)
- Contains state associated with a tooltip. You’ll only need this struct if you’re implementing
tooltip behavior on a custom element. Otherwise, use [Div::tooltip](https://docs.rs/struct.Interactivity.html#method.tooltip).
- [AnyView](https://docs.rs/struct.AnyView.html)
- A dynamically-typed handle to a view, which can be downcast to a [Entity](https://docs.rs/struct.Entity.html)for a specific type.
- [AnyWeak](https://docs.rs/struct.AnyWeakEntity.html)- Entity
- A type erased, weak reference to a entity.
- [AnyWeak](https://docs.rs/struct.AnyWeakView.html)- View
- A weak, dynamically-typed view handle that does not prevent the view from being released.
- [AnyWindow](https://docs.rs/struct.AnyWindowHandle.html)- Handle
- A handle to a window with any root view type, which can be downcast to a window with a specific root view type.
- [App](https://docs.rs/struct.App.html)
- Contains the state of the full application, and passed as a reference to a variety of callbacks.
Other [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)derefs to this type. You need a reference to an`App`to access the state of a[Entity](https://docs.rs/struct.Entity.html).
- [Application](https://docs.rs/struct.Application.html)
- A reference to a GPUI application, typically constructed in the `main`function of your app. You won’t interact with this type much outside of initial configuration and startup.
- [Arena](https://docs.rs/struct.ArenaClearNeeded.html)- Clear - Needed
- Returned when the element arena has been used and so must be cleared before the next draw.
- [Async](https://docs.rs/struct.AsyncApp.html)- App
- An async-friendly version of [App](https://docs.rs/struct.App.html)with a static lifetime so it can be held across`await`points in async code. You’re provided with an instance when calling[App::spawn](https://docs.rs/struct.App.html#method.spawn), and you can also create one with[App::to_async](https://docs.rs/struct.App.html#method.to_async). Internally, this holds a weak reference to an`App`, so its methods are fallible to protect against cases where the[App](https://docs.rs/struct.App.html)is dropped.
- [Async](https://docs.rs/struct.AsyncWindowContext.html)- Window - Context
- A cloneable, owned handle to the application context, composed with the window associated with the current task.
- [Background](https://docs.rs/struct.Background.html)
- A background color, which can be either a solid color or a linear gradient.
- [Background](https://docs.rs/struct.BackgroundExecutor.html)- Executor
- A pointer to the executor that is currently running, for spawning background tasks.
- [Binding](https://docs.rs/struct.BindingIndex.html)- Index
- Index of a binding within a keymap.
- [Boundary](https://docs.rs/struct.Boundary.html)
- A boundary between two lines of text.
- [Bounds](https://docs.rs/struct.Bounds.html)
- Represents a rectangular area in a 2D space with an origin point and a size.
- [Bounds](https://docs.rs/struct.BoundsRefinement.html)- Refinement
- A refinable version of [`#ident`], see that documentation for details.
- [BoxShadow](https://docs.rs/struct.BoxShadow.html)
- The possible values of the box-shadow property
- [Canvas](https://docs.rs/struct.Canvas.html)
- A canvas element, meant for accessing the low level paint API without defining a whole custom element
- [Capslock](https://docs.rs/struct.Capslock.html)
- The state of the capslock key at some point in time
- [Cascade](https://docs.rs/struct.Cascade.html)
- A cascade of refinements that can be merged in priority order.
- [Cascade](https://docs.rs/struct.CascadeSlot.html)- Slot
- A handle to a specific slot in a cascade.
- [Clipboard](https://docs.rs/struct.ClipboardItem.html)- Item
- A clipboard item that should be copied to the clipboard
- [Clipboard](https://docs.rs/struct.ClipboardString.html)- String
- A clipboard item that should be copied to the clipboard
- [Content](https://docs.rs/struct.ContentMask.html)- Mask
- Indicates which region of the window is visible. Content falling outside of this mask will not be rendered. Currently, only rectangular content masks are supported, but we give the mask its own type to leave room to support more complex shapes in the future.
- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)
- The app context, with specialized behavior for the given entity.
- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextEntry.html)- Entry
- An entry in a KeyContext
- [Corners](https://docs.rs/struct.Corners.html)
- Represents the corners of a box in a 2D space, such as border radius.
- [Corners](https://docs.rs/struct.CornersRefinement.html)- Refinement
- A refinable version of [`#ident`], see that documentation for details.
- [Debug](https://docs.rs/struct.DebugBelow.html)- Below
- Use this struct for interfacing with the ‘debug_below’ styling from your own elements. If a parent element has this style set on it, then this struct will be set as a global in GPUI.
- [Decoration](https://docs.rs/struct.DecorationRun.html)- Run
- Set the text decoration for a run of text.
- [Deferred](https://docs.rs/struct.Deferred.html)
- An element which delays the painting of its child until after all of its ancestors, while keeping its layout as part of the current element tree.
- [Deferred](https://docs.rs/struct.DeferredScrollToItem.html)- Scroll - ToItem
- [Device](https://docs.rs/struct.DevicePixels.html)- Pixels
- Represents physical pixels on the display.
- [Dismiss](https://docs.rs/struct.DismissEvent.html)- Event
- Emitted by implementers of `ManagedView`
- [Display](https://docs.rs/struct.DisplayId.html)- Id
- An opaque identifier for a hardware display
- [Div](https://docs.rs/struct.Div.html)
- A `Div`
- [DivFrame](https://docs.rs/struct.DivFrameState.html)- State
- A frame state for a `Div`element, which contains layout IDs for its children.
- [DivInspector](https://docs.rs/struct.DivInspectorState.html)- State
- Interactivity state displayed an manipulated in the inspector.
- [Drag](https://docs.rs/struct.DragMoveEvent.html)- Move - Event
- An event for when a drag is moving over this element, with the given state type.
- [Drawable](https://docs.rs/struct.Drawable.html)
- A wrapper around an implementer of `Element`
- [Dummy](https://docs.rs/struct.DummyKeyboardMapper.html)- Keyboard - Mapper
- A dummy implementation of the platform keyboard mapper
- [Edges](https://docs.rs/struct.Edges.html)
- Represents the edges of a box in a 2D space, such as padding or margin.
- [Edges](https://docs.rs/struct.EdgesRefinement.html)- Refinement
- A refinable version of [`#ident`], see that documentation for details.
- [Element](https://docs.rs/struct.ElementClickedState.html)- Clicked - State
- Whether or not the element or a group that contains it is clicked by the mouse.
- [Element](https://docs.rs/struct.ElementInputHandler.html)- Input - Handler
- The canonical implementation of [`crate::PlatformInputHandler`]. Call`Window::handle_input`
- [Empty](https://docs.rs/struct.Empty.html)
- The empty element, which renders nothing.
- [Empty](https://docs.rs/struct.EmptyView.html)- View
- A view that renders nothing
- [Entity](https://docs.rs/struct.Entity.html)
- A strong, well-typed reference to a struct which is managed by GPUI
- [Entity](https://docs.rs/struct.EntityId.html)- Id
- A unique identifier for a entity across the application.
- [External](https://docs.rs/struct.ExternalPaths.html)- Paths
- A collection of paths from the platform, such as from a file drop.
- [Fallback](https://docs.rs/struct.FallbackPromptRenderer.html)- Prompt - Renderer
- The default GPUI fallback for rendering prompts, when the platform doesn’t support it.
- [Fill](https://docs.rs/struct.FillOptions.html)- Options
- Parameters for the fill tessellator.
- [Focus](https://docs.rs/struct.FocusHandle.html)- Handle
- A handle which can be used to track and manipulate the focused element in a window.
- [FocusId](https://docs.rs/struct.FocusId.html)
- A globally unique identifier for a focusable element.
- [Focus](https://docs.rs/struct.FocusOutEvent.html)- OutEvent
- This is provided when subscribing for `Context::on_focus_out`events.
- [Font](https://docs.rs/struct.Font.html)
- The configuration details for identifying a specific font.
- [Font](https://docs.rs/struct.FontFallbacks.html)- Fallbacks
- The fallback fonts that can be configured for a given font. Fallback fonts family names are stored here.
- [Font](https://docs.rs/struct.FontFamilyId.html)- Family - Id
- An opaque identifier for a specific font family.
- [Font](https://docs.rs/struct.FontFeatures.html)- Features
- The OpenType features that can be configured for a given font.
- [FontId](https://docs.rs/struct.FontId.html)
- An opaque identifier for a specific font.
- [Font](https://docs.rs/struct.FontMetrics.html)- Metrics
- A struct for storing font metrics. It is used to define the measurements of a typeface.
- [FontRun](https://docs.rs/struct.FontRun.html)
- A run of text with a single font.
- [Font](https://docs.rs/struct.FontWeight.html)- Weight
- The degree of blackness or stroke thickness of a font. This value ranges from 100.0 to 900.0, with 400.0 as normal.
- [Foreground](https://docs.rs/struct.ForegroundExecutor.html)- Executor
- A pointer to the executor that is currently running, for spawning tasks on the main thread.
- [Global](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobalElementId.html)- Element - Id
- A globally unique identifier for an element, used to track state across frames.
- [GlyphId](https://docs.rs/struct.GlyphId.html)
- An identifier for a specific glyph, as returned by `WindowTextSystem::layout_line`
- [GpuSpecs](https://docs.rs/struct.GpuSpecs.html)
- Information about the GPU GPUI is running on.
- [Gpui](https://docs.rs/struct.GpuiBorrow.html)- Borrow
- A mutable reference to an entity owned by GPUI
- [Grid](https://docs.rs/struct.GridLocation.html)- Location
- A location in a grid layout.
- [Group](https://docs.rs/struct.GroupStyle.html)- Style
- The styling information for a given group.
- [Highlight](https://docs.rs/struct.HighlightStyle.html)- Style
- A highlight style to apply, similar to a `TextStyle`except for a single font, uniformly sized and spaced text.
- [Hitbox](https://docs.rs/struct.Hitbox.html)
- A rectangular region that potentially blocks hitboxes inserted prior.
See [Window::insert_hitbox](https://docs.rs/struct.Window.html#method.insert_hitbox)for more details.
- [Hitbox](https://docs.rs/struct.HitboxId.html)- Id
- An identifier for a [Hitbox](https://docs.rs/struct.Hitbox.html)which also includes[HitboxBehavior](https://docs.rs/enum.HitboxBehavior.html).
- [Hsla](https://docs.rs/struct.Hsla.html)
- An HSLA color
- [Image](https://docs.rs/struct.Image.html)
- An image, with a format and certain bytes
- [Image](https://docs.rs/struct.ImageCacheElement.html)- Cache - Element
- An image cache element.
- [Image](https://docs.rs/struct.ImageFormatIter.html)- Format - Iter
- An iterator over the variants of [ImageFormat](https://docs.rs/enum.ImageFormat.html)
- [ImageId](https://docs.rs/struct.ImageId.html)
- A unique identifier for the image cache
- [Image](https://docs.rs/struct.ImageStyle.html)- Style
- The style of an image element.
- [Img](https://docs.rs/struct.Img.html)
- An image element.
- [ImgLayout](https://docs.rs/struct.ImgLayoutState.html)- State
- The image layout state between frames
- [Inspector](https://docs.rs/struct.Inspector.html)
- Manages inspector state - which element is currently selected and whether the inspector is in picking mode.
- [Inspector](https://docs.rs/struct.InspectorElementId.html)- Element - Id
- A unique identifier for an element that can be inspected.
- [Inspector](https://docs.rs/struct.InspectorElementPath.html)- Element - Path
- `GlobalElementId`qualified by source location of element construction.
- [Interactive](https://docs.rs/struct.InteractiveElementState.html)- Element - State
- The per-frame state of an interactive element. Used for tracking stateful interactions like clicks and scroll offsets.
- [Interactive](https://docs.rs/struct.InteractiveText.html)- Text
- A text element that can be interacted with.
- [Interactivity](https://docs.rs/struct.Interactivity.html)
- The interactivity struct. Powers all of the general-purpose
interactivity in the `Div`element.
- [Invalid](https://docs.rs/struct.InvalidKeystrokeError.html)- Keystroke - Error
- Error type for `Keystroke::parse`. This is used instead of`anyhow::Error`so that Zed can use markdown to display it.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemSize.html)- Size
- The size of the item and its contents.
- [KeyBinding](https://docs.rs/struct.KeyBinding.html)
- A keybinding and its associated metadata, from the keymap.
- [KeyBinding](https://docs.rs/struct.KeyBindingMetaIndex.html)- Meta - Index
- A unique identifier for retrieval of metadata associated with a key binding. Intended to be used as an index or key into a user-defined store of metadata associated with the binding, such as the source of the binding.
- [KeyContext](https://docs.rs/struct.KeyContext.html)
- A datastructure for resolving whether an action should be dispatched at this point in the element tree. Contains a set of identifiers and/or key value pairs representing the current context for the keymap.
- [KeyDown](https://docs.rs/struct.KeyDownEvent.html)- Event
- The key down event equivalent for the platform.
- [KeyUp](https://docs.rs/struct.KeyUpEvent.html)- Event
- The key up event equivalent for the platform.
- [Keybinding](https://docs.rs/struct.KeybindingKeystroke.html)- Keystroke
- Represents a keystroke that can be used in keybindings and displayed to the user.
- [Keyboard](https://docs.rs/struct.KeyboardClickEvent.html)- Click - Event
- A click event that was generated by a keyboard button being pressed and released.
- [Keymap](https://docs.rs/struct.Keymap.html)
- A collection of key bindings for the user’s application.
- [Keymap](https://docs.rs/struct.KeymapVersion.html)- Version
- An opaque identifier of which version of the keymap is currently active. The keymap’s version is changed whenever bindings are added or removed.
- [Keystroke](https://docs.rs/struct.Keystroke.html)
- A keystroke and associated metadata generated by the platform
- [Keystroke](https://docs.rs/struct.KeystrokeEvent.html)- Event
- A keystroke event, and potentially the associated action
- [Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.LayoutId.html)- Id
- A unique identifier for a layout node, generated when requesting a layout from Taffy
- [Line](https://docs.rs/struct.LineLayout.html)- Layout
- A laid out and styled line of text
- [Line](https://docs.rs/struct.LineWrapper.html)- Wrapper
- The GPUI line wrapper, used to wrap lines of text to a given width.
- [Line](https://docs.rs/struct.LineWrapperHandle.html)- Wrapper - Handle
- A handle into the text system, which can be used to compute the wrapped layout of text
- [Linear](https://docs.rs/struct.LinearColorStop.html)- Color - Stop
- A color stop in a linear gradient.
- [List](https://docs.rs/struct.List.html)
- A list element
- [List](https://docs.rs/struct.ListOffset.html)- Offset
- An offset into the list’s items, in terms of the item index and the number of pixels off the top left of the item.
- [List](https://docs.rs/struct.ListPrepaintState.html)- Prepaint - State
- Frame state used by the [List](https://docs.rs/struct.List.html)element after layout.
- [List](https://docs.rs/struct.ListScrollEvent.html)- Scroll - Event
- A scroll event that has been converted to be in terms of the list’s items.
- [List](https://docs.rs/struct.ListState.html)- State
- The list state that views must hold on behalf of the list element.
- [Menu](https://docs.rs/struct.Menu.html)
- A menu of the application, either a main menu or a submenu

- The state of the modifier keys at some point in time
- [Modifiers](https://docs.rs/struct.ModifiersChangedEvent.html)- Changed - Event
- The modifiers changed event equivalent for the platform.

- A mouse down event from the platform
- [Mouse](https://docs.rs/struct.MouseExitEvent.html)- Exit - Event
- A mouse exit event from the platform, generated when the mouse leaves the window.

- A mouse move event from the platform
- [Mouse](https://docs.rs/struct.MouseUpEvent.html)- UpEvent
- A mouse up event from the platform
- [NoAction](https://docs.rs/struct.NoAction.html)

- OS menus are menus that are recognized by the operating system This allows the operating system to provide specialized items for these menus

- A menu of the application, either a main menu or a submenu

- OS menus are menus that are recognized by the operating system This allows the operating system to provide specialized items for these menus

Passed as an argument `Window::paint_quad`

- A refinable version of [`#ident`], see that documentation for details.

- A handle to a prompt that can be used to interact with it.
- [Prompt](https://docs.rs/struct.PromptResponse.html)- Response
- The event emitted when a prompt’s option is selected. The usize is the index of the selected option, from the actions passed to the prompt.

- Represents an angle in Radians
- [Rems](https://docs.rs/struct.Rems.html)

Allows you to obtain the[EntityId](https://docs.rs/struct.EntityId.html)for a entity before it is created.
- [Retain](https://docs.rs/struct.RetainAllImageCache.html)- AllImage - Cache
- An implementation of ImageCache, that uses an LRU caching strategy to unload images when the cache is full
- [Retain](https://docs.rs/struct.RetainAllImageCacheProvider.html)- AllImage - Cache - Provider

- [Rgba](https://docs.rs/struct.Rgba.html)

- Represents scaled pixels that take into account the device’s scale factor.

- A frame of video captured from a screen.
- [Scroll](https://docs.rs/struct.ScrollAnchor.html)- Anchor
- Represents an element that can be scrolled *to*in its parent element. Contrary to[ScrollHandle::scroll_to_active_item](https://docs.rs/struct.ScrollHandle.html#method.scroll_to_active_item), an anchored element does not have to be an immediate child of the parent.
- [Scroll](https://docs.rs/struct.ScrollHandle.html)- Handle
- A handle to the scrollable aspects of an element. Used for accessing scroll state, like the current scroll offset, and for mutating the scroll state, like scrolling to a specific child.
- [Scroll](https://docs.rs/struct.ScrollWheelEvent.html)- Wheel - Event
- A mouse wheel event from the platform

- A run of text that has been shaped .

- [Shared](https://docs.rs/struct.SharedUri.html)- Uri

- How to truncate text that overflows the width of the element
- [Touch](https://docs.rs/enum.TouchPhase.html)- Phase
- The phase of a touch motion event. Based on the winit enum of the same name.
- [Visibility](https://docs.rs/enum.Visibility.html)
- The value of the visibility property, similar to the CSS property `visibility`
- [White](https://docs.rs/enum.WhiteSpace.html)- Space
- How to handle whitespace in text
- [Window](https://docs.rs/enum.WindowAppearance.html)- Appearance
- The appearance of the window, as defined by the operating system.
- [Window](https://docs.rs/enum.WindowBackgroundAppearance.html)- Background - Appearance
- The appearance of the background of the window itself, when there is no content or the content is transparent.
- [Window](https://docs.rs/enum.WindowBounds.html)- Bounds
- Represents the status of how a window should be opened.
- [Window](https://docs.rs/enum.WindowControlArea.html)- Control - Area
- A type of window control area that corresponds to the platform window.
- [Window](https://docs.rs/enum.WindowDecorations.html)- Decorations
- A type to describe the appearance of a window
- [Window](https://docs.rs/enum.WindowKind.html)- Kind
- The kind of window to create

- [KEYSTROKE_](https://docs.rs/constant.KEYSTROKE_PARSE_EXPECTED_MESSAGE.html)- PARSE_ - EXPECTED_ - MESSAGE

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Action](https://docs.rs/trait.Action.html)
- Actions are used to implement keyboard-driven UI. When you declare an action, you can bind keys to the action in the keymap and listeners for that action in the element tree.
- [Along](https://docs.rs/trait.Along.html)
- A trait for accessing the given unit along a certain axis.
- [Animation](https://docs.rs/trait.AnimationExt.html)- Ext
- An extension trait for adding the animation wrapper to both Elements and Components
- [AppContext](https://docs.rs/trait.AppContext.html)
- The context trait, allows the different contexts in GPUI to be used interchangeably for certain operations.
- [AsKeystroke](https://docs.rs/trait.AsKeystroke.html)
- This is a helper trait so that we can simplify the implementation of some functions
- [Asset](https://docs.rs/trait.Asset.html)
- A trait for asynchronous asset loading.
- [Asset](https://docs.rs/trait.AssetSource.html)- Source
- A source of assets for this app to use.
- [Borrow](https://docs.rs/trait.BorrowAppContext.html)- AppContext
- A helper trait for auto-implementing certain methods on contexts that can be used interchangeably.
- [Element](https://docs.rs/trait.Element.html)
- Implemented by types that participate in laying out and painting the contents of a window. Elements form a tree and are laid out according to web-based layout rules, as implemented by Taffy. You can create custom elements by implementing this trait, see the module-level documentation for more details.
- [Entity](https://docs.rs/trait.EntityInputHandler.html)- Input - Handler
- Implement this trait to allow views to handle textual input when implementing an editor, field, etc.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/trait.EventEmitter.html)- Emitter
- A trait for tying together the types of a GPUI entity and the events it can emit.
- [Flatten](https://docs.rs/trait.Flatten.html)
- A flatten equivalent for anyhow `Result`s.
- [Focusable](https://docs.rs/trait.Focusable.html)
- Focusable allows users of your view to easily focus it (using window.focus_view(cx, view))
- [Future](https://docs.rs/trait.FutureExt.html)- Ext
- Extensions for Future types that provide additional combinators and utilities.
- [Global](https://docs.rs/trait.Global.html)
- A marker trait for types that can be stored in GPUI’s global state.
- [Half](https://docs.rs/trait.Half.html)
- Provides a trait for types that can calculate half of their value.
- [Image](https://docs.rs/trait.ImageCache.html)- Cache
- An object that can handle the caching and unloading of images. Implementations of this trait should ensure that images are removed from all windows when they are no longer needed.
- [Image](https://docs.rs/trait.ImageCacheProvider.html)- Cache - Provider
- An object that can create an ImageCache during the render phase. See the ImageCache trait for more information.
- [Input](https://docs.rs/trait.InputEvent.html)- Event
- An event from a platform input source.
- [Input](https://docs.rs/trait.InputHandler.html)- Handler
- Zed’s interface for handling text input from the platform’s IME system This is currently a 1:1 exposure of the NSTextInputClient API:
- [Interactive](https://docs.rs/trait.InteractiveElement.html)- Element
- A trait for elements that want to use the standard GPUI event handlers that don’t require any state.
- [Into](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoElement.html)- Element
- Implemented by any type that can be converted into an element.
- [IsEmpty](https://docs.rs/trait.IsEmpty.html)
- [IsZero](https://docs.rs/trait.IsZero.html)
- A trait for checking if a value is zero.
- [KeyEvent](https://docs.rs/trait.KeyEvent.html)
- A key event from the platform.
- [Managed](https://docs.rs/trait.ManagedView.html)- View
- ManagedView is a view (like a Modal, Popover, Menu, etc.) where the lifecycle of the view is handled by another view.
- [Mouse](https://docs.rs/trait.MouseEvent.html)- Event
- A mouse event from the platform.
- [Negate](https://docs.rs/trait.Negate.html)
- Provides a trait for types that can negate their values.
- [Parent](https://docs.rs/trait.ParentElement.html)- Element
- This is a helper trait to provide a uniform interface for constructing elements that can accept any number of any kind of child elements
- [Platform](https://docs.rs/trait.PlatformDisplay.html)- Display
- A handle to a platform’s display, e.g. a monitor or laptop screen.
- [Platform](https://docs.rs/trait.PlatformKeyboardLayout.html)- Keyboard - Layout
- A trait for platform-specific keyboard layouts
- [Platform](https://docs.rs/trait.PlatformKeyboardMapper.html)- Keyboard - Mapper
- A trait for platform-specific keyboard mappings
- [Prompt](https://docs.rs/trait.Prompt.html)

- [Read](https://docs.rs/trait.ReadGlobal.html)- Global

- [Refineable](https://docs.rs/trait.Refineable.html)
- A trait for types that can be refined with partial updates.
- [Render](https://docs.rs/trait.Render.html)
- An object that can be drawn to the screen. This is the trait that distinguishes “views” from
other entities. Views are `Entity`’s which`impl Render`and drawn to the screen.
- [Render](https://docs.rs/trait.RenderOnce.html)- Once
- You can derive `IntoElement``components`out of plain data. Think of components as a recipe for a certain pattern of elements. RenderOnce allows you to invoke this pattern, without breaking the fluent builder pattern of the element APIs.
- [Screen](https://docs.rs/trait.ScreenCaptureSource.html)- Capture - Source

- [Styled](https://docs.rs/trait.Styled.html)

- [Visual](https://docs.rs/trait.VisualContext.html)- Context

# wry - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wry/^0.55/

## Expand description

Wry is a cross-platform WebView rendering library.

The webview requires a running event loop and a window type that implements [ HasWindowHandle](https://docs.rs/raw-window-handle/0.6.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/raw_window_handle/borrowed/trait.HasWindowHandle.html),
or a gtk container widget if you need to support X11 and Wayland.
You can use a windowing library like

[or](https://docs.rs/tao)

`tao`[.](https://docs.rs/winit)

`winit`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

This example leverages the [ HasWindowHandle](https://docs.rs/raw-window-handle/0.6.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/raw_window_handle/borrowed/trait.HasWindowHandle.html) and supports Windows, macOS, iOS, Android and Linux (X11 Only).
See the following example using

[:](https://docs.rs/winit)

`winit````
#[derive(Default)]
struct App {
  window: Option<Window>,
  webview: Option<wry::WebView>,
}
impl ApplicationHandler for App {
  fn resumed(&mut self, event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop) {
    let window = event_loop.create_window(Window::default_attributes()).unwrap();
    let webview = WebViewBuilder::new()
      .with_url("https://tauri.app")
      .build(&window)
      .unwrap();
    self.window = Some(window);
    self.webview = Some(webview);
  }
  fn window_event(&mut self, _event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop, _window_id: WindowId, event: WindowEvent) {}
}
let event_loop = EventLoop::new().unwrap();
let mut app = App::default();
event_loop.run_app(&mut app).unwrap();
```
If you also want to support Wayland too, then we recommend you use [`WebViewBuilderExtUnix::new_gtk`] on Linux.
See the following example using [ tao](https://docs.rs/tao):

```
let event_loop = EventLoop::new();
let window = WindowBuilder::new().build(&event_loop).unwrap();
let builder = WebViewBuilder::new().with_url("https://tauri.app");
#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
let webview = builder.build(&window).unwrap();
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
let webview = builder.build_gtk(window.gtk_window()).unwrap();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#child-webviews)Child webviews

You can use [ WebViewBuilder::build_as_child](https://docs.rs/struct.WebViewBuilder.html#method.build_as_child) to create the webview as a child inside another window. This is supported on
macOS, Windows and Linux (X11 Only).

```
#[derive(Default)]
struct App {
  window: Option<Window>,
  webview: Option<wry::WebView>,
}
impl ApplicationHandler for App {
  fn resumed(&mut self, event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop) {
    let window = event_loop.create_window(Window::default_attributes()).unwrap();
    let webview = WebViewBuilder::new()
      .with_url("https://tauri.app")
      .with_bounds(Rect {
        position: LogicalPosition::new(100, 100).into(),
        size: LogicalSize::new(200, 200).into(),
      })
      .build_as_child(&window)
      .unwrap();
    self.window = Some(window);
    self.webview = Some(webview);
  }
  fn window_event(&mut self, _event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop, _window_id: WindowId, event: WindowEvent) {}
}
let event_loop = EventLoop::new().unwrap();
let mut app = App::default();
event_loop.run_app(&mut app).unwrap();
```
If you want to support X11 and Wayland at the same time, we recommend using
[ WebViewExtUnix::new_gtk](https://docs.rs/trait.WebViewExtUnix.html#tymethod.new_gtk) or [

`WebViewBuilderExtUnix::new_gtk`] with [.](https://docs.rs/gtk/0.18.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gtk/auto/fixed/struct.Fixed.html)

`gtk::Fixed````
let event_loop = EventLoop::new();
let window = WindowBuilder::new().build(&event_loop).unwrap();
let builder = WebViewBuilder::new()
  .with_url("https://tauri.app")
  .with_bounds(Rect {
    position: LogicalPosition::new(100, 100).into(),
    size: LogicalSize::new(200, 200).into(),
  });
#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
let webview = builder.build_as_child(&window).unwrap();
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
let webview = {
  let vbox = window.default_vbox().unwrap(); // tao adds a gtk::Box by default
  let fixed = gtk::Fixed::new();
  fixed.show_all();
  vbox.pack_start(&fixed, true, true, 0);
  builder.build_gtk(&fixed).unwrap()
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#platform-considerations)Platform Considerations

Here is the underlying web engine each platform uses, and some dependencies you might need to install.

[§](https://docs.rs#linux)Linux

[WebKitGTK](https://webkitgtk.org/) is used to provide webviews on Linux which requires GTK,
so if the windowing library doesn’t support GTK (as in [ winit](https://docs.rs/winit))
you’ll need to call

[before creating the webview and then call](https://docs.rs/gtk/0.18.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gtk/rt/fn.init.html)

`gtk::init`[alongside your windowing library event loop.](https://docs.rs/gtk/0.18.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gtk/auto/functions/fn.main_iteration_do.html)

`gtk::main_iteration_do````
#[derive(Default)]
struct App {
  webview_window: Option<(Window, WebView)>,
}
impl ApplicationHandler for App {
  fn resumed(&mut self, event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop) {
    let window = event_loop.create_window(Window::default_attributes()).unwrap();
    let webview = WebViewBuilder::new()
      .with_url("https://tauri.app")
      .build(&window)
      .unwrap();
    self.webview_window = Some((window, webview));
  }
  fn window_event(&mut self, _event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop, _window_id: WindowId, event: WindowEvent) {}
  // Advance GTK event loop <!----- IMPORTANT
  fn about_to_wait(&mut self, _event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop) {
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    while gtk::events_pending() {
      gtk::main_iteration_do(false);
    }
  }
}
let event_loop = EventLoop::new().unwrap();
let mut app = App::default();
event_loop.run_app(&mut app).unwrap();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#linux-dependencies)Linux Dependencies

[§](https://docs.rs#arch-linux--manjaro)Arch Linux / Manjaro:

`sudo pacman -S webkit2gtk-4.1`[§](https://docs.rs#debian--ubuntu)Debian / Ubuntu:

`sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev`[§](https://docs.rs#fedora)Fedora

`sudo dnf install gtk3-devel webkit2gtk4.1-devel`[§](https://docs.rs#nix--nixos)Nix & NixOS

```
# shell.nix
let
   # Unstable Channel | Rolling Release
   pkgs = import (fetchTarball("channel:nixpkgs-unstable")) { };
   packages = with pkgs; [
     pkg-config
     webkitgtk_4_1
   ];
 in
 pkgs.mkShell {
   buildInputs = packages;
 }
```
`nix-shell shell.nix`[§](https://docs.rs#guix)GUIX

```
;; manifest.scm
(specifications->manifest
  '("pkg-config"                ; Helper tool used when compiling
    "webkitgtk"                 ; Web content engine fot GTK+
 ))
```
`guix shell -m manifest.scm`[§](https://docs.rs#macos)macOS

WebKit is native on macOS so everything should be fine.

If you are cross-compiling for macOS using [osxcross](https://github.com/tpoechtrager/osxcross) and encounter a runtime panic like `Class with name WKWebViewConfiguration could not be found` it’s possible that `WebKit.framework` has not been linked correctly, to fix this set the `RUSTFLAGS` environment variable:

`RUSTFLAGS="-l framework=WebKit" cargo build --target=x86_64-apple-darwin --release`[§](https://docs.rs#windows)Windows

WebView2 provided by Microsoft Edge Chromium is used. So wry supports Windows 7, 8, 10 and 11.

[§](https://docs.rs#android)Android

In order for `wry` to be able to create webviews on Android, there are a few requirements that your application needs to uphold:

- You need to set a few environment variables that will be used to generate the necessary kotlin
files that you need to include in your Android application for wry to function properly.
- `WRY_ANDROID_PACKAGE`: which is the reversed domain name of your android project and the app name in snake_case, for example,- `com.wry.example.wry_app`
- `WRY_ANDROID_LIBRARY`: for example, if your cargo project has a lib name- `wry_app`, it will generate- `libwry_app.so`so you set this env var to- `wry_app`
- `WRY_ANDROID_KOTLIN_FILES_OUT_DIR`: for example,- `path/to/app/src/main/kotlin/com/wry/example`

- Your main Android Activity needs to inherit `AppCompatActivity`, preferably it should use the generated`WryActivity`or inherit it.
- Your Rust app needs to call `wry::android_setup`function to setup the necessary logic to be able to create webviews later on.
- Your Rust app needs to call `wry::android_binding!`macro to setup the JNI functions that will be called by`WryActivity`and various other places.

It is recommended to use the [ tao](https://docs.rs/tao/latest/tao/) crate as it provides maximum compatibility with

`wry`.```
#[cfg(target_os = "android")]
{
  tao::android_binding!(
      com_example,
      wry_app,
      WryActivity,
      wry::android_setup, // pass the wry::android_setup function to tao which will be invoked when the event loop is created
      _start_app
  );
  wry::android_binding!(com_example, ttt);
}
```
If this feels overwhelming, you can just use the preconfigured template from [ cargo-mobile2](https://github.com/tauri-apps/cargo-mobile2).

For more information, check out [MOBILE.md](https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/blob/dev/MOBILE.md).

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

Wry uses a set of feature flags to toggle several advanced features.

- `os-webview`(default): Enables the default WebView framework on the platform. This must be enabled for the crate to work. This feature was added in preparation of other ports like cef and servo.
- `protocol`(default): Enables- `WebViewBuilder::with_custom_protocol`
- `drag-drop`(default): Enables- `WebViewBuilder::with_drag_drop_handler`
- `devtools`: Enables devtools on release builds. Devtools are always enabled in debug builds. On- **macOS**, enabling devtools, requires calling private APIs so you should not enable this flag in release build if your app needs to publish to App Store.
- `transparent`: Transparent background on- **macOS**requires calling private functions. Avoid this in release build if your app needs to publish to App Store.
- `fullscreen`: Fullscreen video and other media on- **macOS**requires calling private functions. Avoid this in release build if your app needs to publish to App Store.
- `linux-body`: Enables body support of custom protocol request on Linux. Requires WebKit2GTK v2.40 or above.
- `tracing`: enables- `tracing`- `evaluate_script`,- `ipc_handler`, and- `custom_protocols`.

# guise - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/guise-ui/0.4.1/target-redirect/guise/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#guise)guise

A Mantine-inspired component library for [gpui](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed).

`guise` provides a themed palette, sizing tokens, and a growing set of
ready-to-use components built on gpui’s `RenderOnce` builder pattern.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use guise::prelude::*;
Stack::new().gap(Size::Md).child(
    Button::new("save", "Save").variant(Variant::Filled),
)
```
Install a [ Theme](https://docs.rs/theme/struct.Theme.html) once at startup, then read it from any component:

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [chart](https://docs.rs/chart/index.html)
- Charts — minimal, axis-free data visuals painted through gpui’s `canvas`.
- [data](https://docs.rs/data/index.html)
- Data display: components that present structured content.
- [editor](https://docs.rs/editor/index.html)
- Multiline text-editor building blocks.
- [feedback](https://docs.rs/feedback/index.html)
- Feedback: components that communicate state to the user.
- [flex](https://docs.rs/flex/index.html)
- Flexbox layout primitives, for people who think in `Row`/`Column`/`Container`/`Expanded`(à la Flutter).
- [input](https://docs.rs/input/index.html)
- Form inputs.
- [layout](https://docs.rs/layout/index.html)
- Layout primitives: vertical `Stack``Group``Center``AppShell``Container``Space`
- [nav](https://docs.rs/nav/index.html)
- Navigation: components for moving around an app, plus a `StatusBar`
- [overlay](https://docs.rs/overlay/index.html)
- Overlays: floating UI that paints above the page.
- [panegroup](https://docs.rs/panegroup/index.html)
- `PaneGroup`— a recursive tree of- **tabbed**panes (splits contain tabs), the Zed / VS Code editor-group workspace model as a reusable gpui component.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Common imports for building with `guise`.
- [reactive](https://docs.rs/reactive/index.html)
- A lightweight, React-flavored state layer over gpui.
- [style](https://docs.rs/style/index.html)
- Shared visual variants. Mantine resolves a `(color, variant)`pair into a background / foreground / border triple that every interactive component (Button, Badge, ActionIcon, …) draws from. This is that resolver.
- [theme](https://docs.rs/theme/index.html)
- The theme: palette + sizing tokens + color scheme, exposed as a gpui
`Global`so any component can resolve themed values during render.
